projects.title: A Strategic Approach to Solving Public Health Challenges

content.text: Design culturally sensitive public health strategies by integrating legal, ethical, and behavioral insights to address real-world health challenges.

Public health policies often fall short when they fail to account for sociocultural and behavioral factors, resulting in interventions that lack equity and cultural sensitivity. In this Build Project, you’ll step into the role of a Public Health Policy Strategist to design culturally competent healthcare strategies. Under the supervision of an experienced healthcare professional, you’ll analyze real-world scenarios to develop actionable policy briefs, infographics, and presentations that integrate ethical, legal, and behavioral insights. You’ll gain hands-on experience in public health policy development, mastering tools and methodologies used to create impactful, equitable solutions. This project offers a unique opportunity to bridge theoretical knowledge with practical applications, preparing you for a meaningful career in public health and health policy.
Learn Core Public Health Concepts: Understand public health policy, law, ethics, and the role of sociocultural factors in shaping health outcomes.
Learn and Apply Research Methods: Practice entry-level research techniques to identify and analyze public health issues.
Draft Actionable Recommendations: Create simple, actionable proposals that reflect public health law, ethics, and community needs.
Communicate Effectively: Develop communication skills to explain public health strategies clearly to peers and stakeholders.
Basic knowledge of public health policy and management: You should understand the fundamentals of healthcare systems, public health initiatives, and health management principles.

Understanding of sociocultural and behavioral factors in healthcare: You should be able to analyze how culture, behavior, and social determinants impact health outcomes. This knowledge is crucial for developing effective, inclusive health strategies.

Communication and presentation skills: You will need to effectively convey your ideas through both written and oral presentations. This includes preparing reports, creating infographics, and delivering concise presentations with clear messaging.
Basic proficiency in data visualization tools: Familiarity with tools like PowerPoint, Canva, or similar software to create visually engaging slides and infographics to communicate your findings.

Critical thinking and problem-solving skills: You should be able to approach complex public health challenges with a solution-oriented mindset, integrating diverse perspectives into your analysis and recommendations.

In this Build Project, you’ll step into the role of a process engineer exploring three leading solar cell technologies: PERC, TOPCon, and HJT. You’ll learn industry practices, process control and characterization method, and get exposure to improvements in process flow. You’ll be introduced to techniques used in modern solar manufacturing like lifetime testing (WCT-120), optical profiling, and others characterization tool. Guided by a professional in the field and with a real case study, you will be more familiar with troubleshooting process bottlenecks and improving solar cell performance—just like engineers do in leading solar manufacturing environments.

projects.title: AI Image Models: Get Started with the Basics

content.text: Discover how machine learning engineers train image models, evaluate their quality, and improve them through fast, repeatable experiment loops.

In the coming years, generative AI will be extremely useful for robotics. Training robots in the real world is prohibitively expensive, so we need simulators. Classical simulators require hardcoding scenarios and do not match real world distributions. We want trained simulators that scale with data and compute.

In this Build Project we’ll build a simple simulator in the form of an image generation model. Training Gen AI models is largely an infrastructure problem. You want tests for the model’s outputs, simple experiment tracking and fast model training. This is the real day-to-day work of ML engineers, so that's what we’ll focus on!

By the end of the 8-weeks project, you will: write one test evaluating the output of an image generation model, run one experiment to try to improve it and write up a report. You are welcome to run this loop as many times as you’d like, to improve your model further, on any axis you find interesting.
Write simple deep learning training code.
Write tests to evaluate deep learning models.
Run experiments and draw conclusions, using Weights&Biases.
Programming experience (i.e. writing a python script that can scrape a website or build a tiny video game).
Basic debugging skills (i.e. knowing how to use the python debugger, finding and reading documentation/datasheets, prompting LLMs).
General computer science skills: git, bash, terminal use.
Interest in AI, simulators and ML.

projects.title: AI-Powered Data Exploration: Build Your Own Analytics Assistant

content.text: Create an intelligent AI Agent that lets you work with your data using plain English instead of code.

The way we work with data is changing. AI is no longer limited to specialized fields, it's becoming a core competency across nearly every industry. Data scientists, engineers, and analysts are increasingly expected to incorporate AI into their workflows. Understanding how AI works under the hood is what makes the difference between using these tools and getting the most out of them. In this Build Project, you'll build that understanding from the ground up, by creating an AI-powered assistant that can explore, analyze, and visualize data through plain English conversation, demystifying AI agents along the way.

You'll start by learning how to control LLM behavior and produce reliable, structured outputs. From there, you'll progressively build an agent that can reason about problems and work with real data through natural conversation. Each week adds a new layer of capability while pulling back the curtain on another piece of how modern AI systems work. By the end of this 8-week project, you'll adapt your agent to a dataset of your choice and build a practical data science application that showcases both your analytical skills and your understanding of AI. You won't just know how to use AI tools, you'll know how they work, and how they are built. By integrating cutting-edge AI into traditional data science workflows, you'll create a powerful assistant that eliminates tedious coding while maintaining full control over your analysis.

This project prepares you for the paradigm shift in software development, where AI collaboration is becoming essential, by building a portfolio piece that proves you're ready for the AI-augmented future of programming.
Understand how Large Language Models and AI agents work under the hood.
Apply prompt engineering techniques to produce reliable, structured outputs from LLMs.
Build an AI agent from the ground up that can explore, analyze, and visualize data through natural conversation.
Adapt your agent to a dataset and domain of your choice, creating a practical data science application.

Experience loading CSV files with pd.read_csv() and using basic pandas commands like df.head() and df.describe().

projects.title: Algorithmic Trading: From Data to Alpha

content.text: Develop a basic, automated trading strategy using Python while learning how professional quantitative analysts uncover hidden opportunities in the stock market.

Algorithmic trading accounts for the vast majority of volume in modern financial markets, yet the mechanics behind these automated systems often seem hidden behind a wall of complex math. In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Quantitative Analyst and build a foundational systematic trading strategy from scratch. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll use Python to analyze historical market data, generate trading signals, apply realistic risk constraints, and calculate execution costs. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real quantitative research desk, giving you practical, hands-on experience in one of the most competitive sectors of finance.

Upon completing this 8-week project, you will walk away with a polished Jupyter Notebook that models a systematic trading strategy—a tangible portfolio piece you can use to impress hiring managers and kickstart your career in quantitative finance.

projects.title: Alpha Lab: Building a Quant Strategy from Real-Time U.S. Equity Data

content.text: Predict short-term price movements in U.S. equities by designing and implementing a quantitative model using real-time market data.

Have you ever wondered how quantitative researchers and data scientists try to predict movements in the stock market? In this project, you will explore one of the most challenging and exciting problems in finance: predicting short-term price movements in U.S. equities. You’ll work with real-time U.S. equity market data, clean and analyze it using Python, and turn raw price and volume information into simple predictive features. From there, you’ll build and test short-term prediction models, evaluate their performance, and learn how professionals decide whether a model is genuinely useful—or just looks good on paper.

Along the way, you’ll encounter challenges that come up all the time in real finance and data science roles, such as imperfect data, overfitting, unstable model performance, and changing market behavior. By tackling these issues hands-on, you’ll build practical skills that translate directly to entry-level roles in quantitative finance, trading, fintech, and data science—while gaining a clearer picture of what working with financial data looks like day to day.

Explain how a quantitative trading strategy is developed from start to finish, and describe how U.S. equity markets work, including short-term price movements, trading volume, and basic order book behavior.
Collect, clean, and analyze real-time U.S. equity market data by building a simple and reliable data pipeline using Python, Pandas, NumPy, and market data APIs.

Create and evaluate quantitative features, such as returns, volatility, and order flow signals, and measure their usefulness using standard performance metrics like Information Coefficient (IC), factor returns, and Sharpe ratio.
Build and test short-term price prediction models using linear regression in Python, applying rolling-window training and walk-forward validation to reduce overfitting and look-ahead bias.

Evaluate and interpret trading model performance using risk-adjusted metrics (e.g., Sharpe ratio, drawdowns, turnover, and PnL after costs), and discuss key limitations, risks, and challenges of using these models in real-world trading.

Proficiency in Python for data analysis, including the ability to manipulate time-indexed, multi-indexed dataframe using Pandas, perform numerical operations with NumPy, visualize portfolio performance and structure multiple plots using Matplotlib, and write modular, reproducible research codes.

Foundational understanding of financial time series, returns, and order book data, including concepts such as log returns, volatility, autocorrelation, non-stationarity, and basic order book structure

Introductory understanding of statistical modeling principles, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, bias-variance tradeoff, overfitting, regularization and importance of out-of-sample validation.

Ability to interpret model results via portfolio performance metrics, including why measures such as cumulative returns, Sharpe ratio, drawdowns, and turnover are more meaningful than raw prediction accuracy in trading contexts.

projects.title: Analyze a Dataset from a Critical Gender Perspective

content.text: Learn gender data best practices and audit a dataset of your choice and create an improved version of the dataset analysis.

In the field of data science, the issue of data equity is an ongoing movement that aims to promote responsible data work. The current problem with major data practices is not that the data we have is insufficient, but that it doesn’t not accurately reflect the realities of women and non-binary people. For example, the gender binary (male/female) classification system in data collection will result in omission errors that make certain people’s experiences invisible. In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Data Analyst and audit data cycle practices with a gender lens. Based on it, you'll produce a data visualization project that incorporates standard visualization frameworks and gender data best practices. Under the supervision of an experienced Build Fellow, you'll uncover the flaws in current research methodologies that have led to inaccurate and incomplete data on the status of women and non-binary persons. You'll explore marginal changes that can be made to the way that we collect, analyze, and visualize gender data. You’ll become familiar with data visualization frameworks such as Tufte’s rules, Junk Chart’s trifecta, and Schwabish’s core principles, as well as such ubiquitous industry tools as Excel, R, or Tableau. b:["$","$L19",
Produce visuals that improve comprehension patterns for sex disaggregated data using standard visualization frameworks and gender data visualization best practices .
Audit data analysis projects using a gender lens and provide practical recommendations from learned best practices of gender data collection, analysis, and visualization .
Develop a data visualization critique and recommend improvements to make gender data visuals more compelling, digestible, ethical, simple, and accurate.
Basic experience working with data: you should know how to read a dataset, clean data, and create a visual.
Basic knowledge of one of data visualization tools (such as Excel, R, Tableau): you should know how to navigate this tool, be able to use a dataset to create and format different visuals.
Other prerequisites: before the project starts, you'll need to have Excel and the data visualization tool of your choice installed on your computer.

projects.title: AWS Cloud Fundamentals: Deploy a Scalable Web Application

content.text: Learn to deploy and scale a simple pre-built web application on AWS using EC2 and ELB to master real-world cloud infrastructure.

In today's technology landscape, nearly every company, from startups to large enterprises, relies on cloud platforms to deliver reliable and scalable digital services. This project gives you crucial, hands-on experience by guiding you through the complete lifecycle of deploying a simple web application onto the Amazon Web Services (AWS) platform using the Free Tier. You will build and configure the entire underlying infrastructure, including setting up secure access with IAM, configuring networking with Security Groups, deploying compute instances, and implementing scalability features. In the process, you will acquire practical knowledge of infrastructure management, resource provisioning, and cloud architecture—highly sought-after technical skills that are essential for entry-level Cloud Engineering, DevOps, and Software Developer roles.
Deploy a scalable web application on the cloud platform.
Design a resilient cloud architecture by implementing identity management, network security, and load-balancing protocols.
Integrate an application with cloud infrastructure to ensure seamless service delivery.
Navigate the professional AWS ecosystem to provision, manage, and monitor live cloud resources in a real-world production environment.
A functional grasp of how data travels across the internet, including the role of IP addressing, subnets, routing, and the structure of data packets.
Competency in Python fundamentals, specifically managing data types, implementing loops, and handling conditional logic to build a simple application.
A clear understanding of the Client-Server model, including how the frontend communicates with the backend via HTTP/HTTPS requests and APIs.

projects.title: Behind the Scenes: How Cities Choose Software

content.text: Build a simplified ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) selection model showing how public organizations align technology choices with city department needs and budgets.

Cities across the country rely on technology to manage finances, human resources, utilities, and citizen services — but choosing the right system is a complex and highly structured process. In this Build Project, you’ll step into the role of a Business Systems Analyst and build a simplified ERP selection model that shows how public organizations align technology choices with departmental needs and budgets. Under the guidance of an experienced municipal systems professional, you’ll analyze workflows, define system requirements, simulate a vendor scorecard, and design a visual infographic that captures the full RFP process. You’ll become familiar with tools and techniques used in public administration and technology management, such as workflow mapping, data visualization, and vendor evaluation, all within a simulated environment that mirrors a real city project team.
Analyze how organizations evaluate and select enterprise software systems to meet operational needs.
Map workflows that show how a public entity selects new software exceeding procurement thresholds that require a formal Request for Proposal (RFP).
Develop a simplified vendor evaluation scorecard to compare technology options using real-world criteria.
Visualize data and decision-making processes through clear, professional dashboards.
Present findings and recommendations using a concise, portfolio-ready format that highlights analytical and communication skills.
Basic knowledge of Excel: You should be able to organize data in tables, apply simple formulas (like SUM or AVERAGE), and create a simple dashboard to summarize information.
Interest in how organizations use technology: You don’t need prior ERP experience, but you should be curious about how departments share data and make software decisions.
Analytical thinking and attention to detail: You’ll compare different software options and evaluate how they meet organizational needs and budgets.
Clear communication and collaboration skills: You’ll work with peers to exchange ideas and present findings visually and verbally in a concise, professional way.
Willingness to learn visualization techniques: You’ll use Canva to transform your analysis and dashboard into a polished, portfolio-ready infographic.

Sara is a Municipal Systems Analyst at the City of Temple Terrace, where she focuses on cross-departmental ERP deployment, workflow automation, and digital transformation using Microsoft 365 tools.

projects.title: Behind the Scenes of Efficiency & Profitability: (Re)Structuring a Film Industry Powerhouse

content.text: Develop a data-driven organizational restructuring plan that enhances efficiency, boosts profitability, and establishes a scalable foundation for rapid growth, maximizing the value of limited resources.

Films are a high-risk, high-reward asset class—and while investing is easy, getting repaid isn’t. To succeed, institutional investors must build private credit funds with world-class operations that maximize efficiency, productivity, and profitability in a fast-paced, resource-constrained industry.

In this Build Project, you’ll take on the role of a senior operations manager at a private credit fund focused on film finance. You’ll assess the organization’s internal workflows, identify inefficiencies, and design a data-driven restructuring plan to improve efficiency, productivity, and scalability. Guided by an industry expert, you’ll use KPIs to evaluate operations and propose practical solutions in a fast-paced, resource-constrained environment. Along the way, you’ll explore how film deals are structured and how institutional funds operate in the entertainment space. You’ll apply change management frameworks—like Kotter’s and Lewin’s change models—to a real-world business case study to build the implementation plan for your restructuring strategy.

Working collaboratively as a single team, you and your peers will assign roles, define responsibilities, and build internal systems and workflows. All deliverables will be produced collectively, and your performance will be evaluated as a group.  By the end, you will build and pitch your C-suite-ready pitch deck to present your re-organizational plan.
Develop in-depth knowledge of the core operations and processes commonly found in finance-based, fund-like organizations, including Private Credit, Venture Capital, and Private Equity firms.
Build a film finance model by structuring its collateral pool to enable access to private credit-type funds demonstrating practical application of financial structuring in the entertainment industry.
Identify and break down a business’s core operations and processes across all departments and functions, establishing a clear understanding of its workflow and interdependencies.
Conduct data-driven analysis using department- and function-specific KPIs to assess, evaluate, and rank operational efficiency, productivity, and profitability.
Design 360-degree, actionable solutions to address inefficiencies through process automation, team restructuring, resource management, and cost-cutting strategies.
Package, present, and deliver comprehensive company-wide restructuring plans, ensuring stakeholder buy-in and effective implementation through structured change management processes.

Fundamentals of Debt Financing: A basic understanding of debt financing principles, including key financial concepts such as collateral, loan-to-value ratios, principal, and interest. You should be comfortable discussing financial structures and evaluating lending risks.

Business and Operations Management: Beginner/Intermediate knowledge of business management, including principles of operations, resource allocation, organizational psychology, and change management. You should understand how to assess and optimize business workflows for efficiency and scalability.

Film Industry Fundamentals: A basic, general foundational understanding of the macroeconomics and mechanics of the film industry, along with a willingness to develop deeper insights into the broader Media & Entertainment sector. This includes familiarity with financing models, market dynamics, and industry hierarchy/politics.

Presentation and Visual Communication: Proficiency in presentation tools such as PowerPoint, Keynote, or Canva to create compelling and visually effective slide decks. Students should be able to structure information clearly and design engaging presentations that effectively convey key insights.

Effective Communication and Persuasion: Strong verbal and written communication skills to articulate ideas clearly and persuasively. This includes the ability to pitch concepts, present findings confidently, and secure stakeholder buy-in through compelling storytelling and structured argumentation.
Beginner knowledge of data analytics with practical experience applying KPIs in business environments to back proposed management solutions.

fellows.name: Luigi Spitaleri

projects.title: Beyond Transactions: Designing Human-Centered Experiences

content.text: Build end-to-end customer experience strategies that enhance satisfaction, operational efficiency, and emotional engagement.

In today’s experience-driven economy, businesses across industries, from luxury hospitality to tech startups, compete not just on product, but on how services make customers feel. In this Build Project, you'll step into the role of a Customer Experience Strategist, working hands-on to design emotionally resonant, end-to-end service journeys that enhance satisfaction, loyalty, and operational effectiveness. Under the guidance of an industry fellow, you’ll apply tools like customer journey mapping, service blueprinting, and empathy mapping to reimagine real-world service systems and co-create value through service innovation. You'll leave the project with a professional-level Experience Strategy Dossier that simulates the work of consulting teams and innovation labs across sectors like hospitality, healthcare, fintech, and luxury retail.
Apply theoretical principles from Service-Dominant Logic (SDL) to understand value co-creation in customer service ecosystems.
Construct detailed Customer Journey Maps and diagnose service failure points using touchpoint analysis.
Develop user personas based on ethnographic interviews and empathy mapping techniques.
Design Service Blueprints to align frontstage customer interactions with backstage operational processes.
Incorporate cognitive-emotional triggers into experiential strategies to optimize client satisfaction and loyalty.
A foundational understanding of service marketing principles (e.g., SERVQUAL, 7Ps framework).
Familiarity with qualitative research methods such as customer interviews, observational techniques, or thematic coding.
Conceptual awareness of UX or HCD (Human-Centered Design) frameworks.
Proficiency in using visual collaboration or prototyping tools (e.g., Miro, Figma, Canva).
Analytical and reflective thinking skills for identifying root causes of service gaps and proposing strategic improvements.

Data Analysis and modelling using Google Sheets

Presentation and Communication through writing diligence reports

projects.title: Bluebeam Revu: Facade Estimation in Construction Projects

content.text: Design a worksheet to estimate the cost of materials, labor, and equipment for building exterior envelopes using real-life projects.

Accurate cost estimating for building exterior envelopes is a core responsibility in construction and preconstruction teams and is a common task assigned to entry-level estimators, project engineers, and preconstruction analysts across the industry. In this Build Project, you’ll step into the role of a Construction Estimator and develop a detailed facade cost estimating worksheet by performing digital quantity takeoffs and organizing material, labor, and equipment costs using real construction documents. Under the guidance of an experienced industry professional, students will actively measure drawings, apply unit pricing, and document estimating assumptions rather than passive learning concepts. Students will become comfortable using industry-standard tools and workflows such as Bluebeam Revu, quantity takeoff methods, and preconstruction cost analysis, all within a learning environment that mirrors the daily operations of a real construction preconstruction and estimating team.
Perform digital quantity takeoffs using Bluebeam Revu
Develop structured cost estimates for exterior envelope systems
Apply real-world unit pricing and productivity rates
Analyze preconstruction cost impacts of design decisions
Communicate estimating assumptions and results clearly
Comfort reading construction drawings: You should be able to look at architectural drawings and understand basic things like exterior walls, dimensions, scales, and notes.

Basic spreadsheet skills (Excel or Google Sheets): You should feel comfortable creating tables, typing numbers, using simple formulas (like adding and multiplying), and organizing information in a spreadsheet. No advanced Excel skills are needed.

Willingness to pay attention to details: Estimating is all about accuracy. You don’t need to be perfect, but you should be willing to slow down, double-check your quantities, and fix small mistakes when you find them.

projects.title: Bonds to Blockchain: A Practitioner's Introduction to Securitized Products

content.text: This project introduces students to capital markets, focusing on fixed income, structured finance, and blockchain applications, culminating in a trade pitch presentation.

This Build Project will introduce you to capital markets by focusing on real-world examples from fixed income and structured finance. You will start by understanding bond mechanics and market roles, then dive into securitization and products like CLOs and RMBS. Midway, you will explore blockchain’s emerging role in finance through DeFi and RWAs. Each workshop builds toward a final presentation where you will pitch a trade idea. The hands-on format and technical tools used (like Excel and Glassnode) will help you build tangible, portfolio-ready work. This project prepares you for entry-level finance and fintech roles by giving you the skills used by analysts, traders, and associates in today's evolving markets.
Explain how capital markets and fixed income products like bonds, RMBS, and CLOs function in the real world
Use Excel to perform a bond duration analysis and assess risk-return trade-offs
Analyze a DeFi protocol and understand the role of Real World Assets (RWAs) on the blockchain
Build and deliver a structured trade pitch based on investor objectives and risk appetite
Develop practical presentation and valuation skills relevant for careers in finance and fintech
A basic understanding of macroeconomic concepts like interest rates, inflation, and market cycles.
Familiarity with Excel and comfort performing calculations like percentages and changes
Willingness to learn financial concepts such as bond pricing, duration, tranching, and yield.
Curiosity about how markets and financial products work and their real-world applications.
Interest in new financial technologies like blockchain and decentralized finance (no prior crypto experience required).

projects.title: Bootstrapping a Treasury Yield Curve

content.text: Master the method to derive precise interest rates for different maturities by leveraging financial modelling techniques.

In this Finance Modeling Project, you'll step into the shoes of a Quantitative Analyst and construct a Treasury Yield Curve from scratch. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll analyze market data and implement a mathematical model in Python to estimate term structures of interest rates. You'll become familiar with industry tools and methodologies for data manipulation and bootstrapping techniques for yield curve construction. All this will provide invaluable hands-on experience crucial for entry-level roles in finance, where proficiency in quantitative modeling and data analysis is highly valued.
Deepen your understanding of fixed income concepts such as par rates, coupons, yield-to-maturity, gaining insights into bond valuation.
Develop proficiency in Python programming, including data manipulation, statistical analysis and visualization using libraries such as Pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib.
Gain knowledge of financial market data sources and APIs for accessing and retrieving relevant financial data for analysis.
Get hands on experience in applying financial modeling techniques for yield curve construction and interpolation.
Experience with Python (loops, conditions, functions, libraries, simple algorithms). Knowledge of Jupyter notebook is a plus.
Understanding of financial concepts like compound interest, coupon rate, par values etc.
Familiarity with statistical techniques such as interpolation, regression and curve fitting.

projects.title: Bridging Science and Policy for Effective Environmental Management

content.text: Develop a policy framework that bridges environmental science and public policy to address uncertainties and knowledge gaps in real-world environmental challenges.

In today’s environmental policy sector, the ability to transform scientific data into actionable, evidence-based policy solutions is a fundamental skill sought after in entry-level roles across government agencies, NGOs, and private companies. In this Build Project, you'll step into the role of an environmental policy analyst and develop practical solutions to real-world challenges like nuclear waste management and lead contamination. Under the guidance of your instructor, you'll analyze scientific research, assess stakeholder concerns, and craft well-informed policy recommendations that balance both environmental and societal needs. You'll become familiar with industry tools and methodologies such as stakeholder mapping and policy analysis frameworks. All this will take place in an environment that mirrors the operations of a real-world environmental policy team, providing hands-on experience in addressing global environmental challenges.
Assess the theoretical and practical complexities at the science-policy interface by exploring real-world environmental cases from government, civil society, and private sector perspectives.
Evaluate and describe the complexity of science-policy relations, developing critical-thinking and communication skills through written assignments and oral presentations.
Collaborate effectively in teams, leveraging complementary knowledge and skills to address real-world environmental challenges and formulate innovative policy solutions.

Understanding of Environmental Science and Policy: Basic understanding of environmental science principles, especially how socio-political factors shape environmental issues such as nuclear waste management and lead pollution.

Research and Analytical Skills: Ability to analyze case studies, evaluate scientific data, assess policy effectiveness, synthesize information from multiple sources, and make evidence-based recommendations.

Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to assess how political, corporate, and social factors influence environmental policies and craft solutions to challenges such as lead contamination and nuclear waste management.

Communication and Advocacy Skills: Ability to clearly articulate analysis in written and verbal forms, advocate for policy solutions, and engage with stakeholders such as media, civil society, and government agencies.

projects.title: Build a Full-Stack Software Application

content.text: Learn how to use PostgreSQL, Typescript, React and Vue to create a software app.

The deliverables for this project are focused on building artifacts that you can use to showcase your work in a job application. By the end of the project, you will have built a full-stack software application that follows multi-tier architecture. You will learn about databases, back-end systems, and front-end systems. You will learn how to build an application that is extensible and complete. The application can do what you wish but must have all the relevant components. At the end of the project, you will deploy your application for anyone on the internet to view. This way, you’ll have something tangible to show recruiters for future job prospects.
Learn how to create a full-stack software application that is thoughtfully designed and visually striking.
Learn the concepts of multi-tier architecture and separation of concerns.

Become familiar with the software development process, Github, databases like PostgreSQL, backend systems written in languages like Typescript, and frontend systems written using modern frameworks like React and Vue.
Commitment to start and finish the project, actively participate in all meetings, and work independently for 2 hours/week.

Basic/intermediate knowledge of programming languages: you should be familiar with at least one language like JavaScript, Python, Java etc. Any introductory level computer science class should cover at least one.
Basic knowledge of command line: Be able to move around files and navigate a computer through the command line.
Basic knowledge of multi-tier architecture is a plus.
Other prerequisites: before the project starts, you will need to be familiar with using git on the command line and have a GitHub account.

projects.title: Build a Graph UI Library to Visualize Data Relations

content.text: Use React and Typescript to develop a Graph UI library that takes a data schema and returns a flow diagram with a depiction of all the data relations in the schema.

In most organizations, data is stored in hundreds or thousands of columns stored in multiple tables. With this level of complexity, it's often hard to understand the relation between tables, columns, views, and workflows. In this Build Project, you'll build a library that takes in a complicated data schema, analyzes all the existing relations, and provide a flow chart as an output to easily understand all the relations and how data flows in the system. All these skills are essential for the productive work of any specialist analyzing large datasets, and in this project, you have a chance to develop them under supervision of an experienced Project Leader.
Expand your knowledge of coding languages, databases, and version control.
Learn how to build a UI library.
Learn how to use git, yarn package manager.
Learn ow to use React and Typescript to build a front-end application.
Commitment to start and finish the project, actively participate in all meetings, and work independently for ~1 hour/week.
Basic understanding of data structures and algorithms.
Basic programming skills: you should know how to works with classes and objects.
Basic understanding of git: you should be able to clone a project, create a branch and push changes to branch.
React and Typescript (coding languages used in this project): prior knowledge is not required, but it's a plus.
Desire to develop your UI and data visualization skills.

projects.title: Build a React Component Library in Chromatic

content.text: Design, document, and ship a reusable React component library using Chromatic, following the same workflow frontend engineers use at modern tech companies.

Frontend development teams at nearly every tech company maintain a shared component library: a toolkit of reusable buttons, inputs, modals, and other UI building blocks that keep products consistent and speed up development. In this Build Project, you'll learn the workflows of a frontend engineer and build your own React component library from scratch, complete with design tokens, interactive Storybook documentation, and automated visual testing through Chromatic. Under the supervision of an experienced software engineer, you'll design and implement 10–15 components in React and TypeScript, document each one in Storybook, and set up a CI pipeline so every push automatically checks for visual regressions. You'll become familiar with industry tools like Storybook, Chromatic, and GitHub Actions, and you'll use AI tools the way engineers actually do: to scaffold boilerplate, generate documentation, and audit accessibility issues. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the day-to-day operations of a real frontend engineering team.b:
Build reusable React/TypeScript UI components using component-driven development principles
Write Storybook stories that document every variant and interactive state of your components, making your library usable by developers who didn't write it
Connect automated visual snapshot testing via Chromatic and a GitHub Actions CI pipeline, so every pull request is reviewed for unintended UI changes
Audit your components for web accessibility using the Storybook a11y addon and apply fixes based on WCAG principles
Apply AI tools (Claude, GitHub Copilot) the way engineers do in industry to scaffold boilerplate, write documentation, and identify issues faster
Experience writing code in at least one programming language: you should be comfortable reading and modifying multi-file projects, even if they're not in JavaScript or TypeScript

projects.title: Build a Real Retrieval-Augmented AI System from Scratch

content.text: Turn raw documents into an intelligent search system that can find answers, summarize content, and power real‑world applications like chatbots and research assistants.

Across today’s software and AI teams, systems that search and organize internal documents power tools like chatbots, research assistants, and knowledge bases. In this project, you’ll build your own AI‑powered question‑answering system from the ground up. Over 8 weeks, you’ll follow the same workflow used in industry: loading and cleaning documents, breaking them into useful chunks, embedding and storing them in a vector database, and retrieving the right information to help a language model answer questions. You’ll use Python, FastAPI, and modern AI tools to create a simple but realistic backend application that reflects how engineers build intelligent search systems today.
Process raw documents into clean, structured text that can be used in an AI workflow.
Analyze how chunking, embeddings, and retrieval affect the quality of search results.
Integrate a vector database and a language model into a document question-answering pipeline.
Design API requests and responses for an AI-powered backend service.
Test and explain the technical decisions behind your system, including retrieval quality, prompting, and API design.
Some experience with Python: you should be comfortable writing functions, using lists and dictionaries, and reading basic class-based code.
Basic understanding of APIs: you should know what a request and response are, even if you have not built a full API before.
Basic command line comfort: you should be able to navigate folders, run Python files, and install packages.
Problem-solving mindset: you should be willing to debug, test small changes, and learn step by step.
Curiosity about how AI systems work: you do not need prior RAG experience, but you should be interested in learning how documents, search, and language models connect.

Use and navigate the ServiceNow platform

projects.title: Build, Train, and Deploy a Transformer Language Model in PyTorch

content.text: Perform cutting-edge natural language processing techniques by coding core architectures, preprocessing real datasets, and evaluating results with Python tools like Jupyter, SpaCy, and matplotlib, culminating in a runnable GPT.

Test With transformers are dominating the machine learning world by setting new benchmarks in various NLP (natural language processing) tasks and Vision tasks. This Build Project will help you learn about transformers, specifically GPT models (which are powering the AI chat assistance like ChatGPT). We will delve into the intricacies of transformer architecture using PyTorch. You will learn to build, train, and deploy GPT models from scratch, understanding their superior capabilities compared to prior NLP baselines. This knowledge is valuable in today’s job market where the demand for AI expertise is rapidly growing.
Acquire familiarity with PyTorch machine learning library, visualization tools like matplotlib and plotly and python programming environment.
Learn how to collect, preprocess, and tokenize text data for training a language model.
Implement and compare baseline models or traditional NLP methods to highlight the improvements offered by transformer-based approaches.
Gain a deep understanding of the components and functioning of transformer models, including self-attention, multi-head attention, and positional encoding.

Develop and train your own character level generative pretrained transformer (GPT) model for specific task like creating Shakespear inspired stories, generating code snippets or composing music lyrics.
Prior programming experience in Python, and experience working with Python tools and environments.
Some first exposure to additional libraries like numpy, pandas and matplotlib.
Familiarity with machine learning concepts like feedforward networks, activation functions, loss functions, and backpropagation.

Familiarity with statistical concepts such as probability distributions and basic understanding of linear algebra, enabling students to understand and interpret the inner workings of the model effectively.

projects.title: Build Smarter: Construction Project Lifecycle & Tech Essentials

content.text: Create a beginner-friendly portfolio of real-world construction documents by defining scope, securing build scheduling permits, and exploring AI tools.

From concept to close‑out, every civil project moves through a predictable set of milestones. In this Build Project you'll step into the shoes of a junior project engineer and walk a mock job through permits, RFIs, inspections, schedules, and earned‑value check‑ins—all while seeing where emerging AI tools can streamline the process. Each session you'll learn the key elements in executing a civil engineering project. By the end, you'll understand the key elements of project execution, know how to build and monitor a simple schedule, and see how new technology is reshaping the civil‑engineering workplace—insights you can showcase in your next internship or co‑op interview.
Identify the three critical starts up elements for any civil project (scope, constraints, stakeholders).
Learn essential preconstruction approvals, including land acquisition, environmental, and permit clearances.
Understand what an RFI (request for information) and submittal are, and how to use them for clear project communication.
Create a draft project schedule & perform Earned Value Management (EVM) analysis.
Discover one emerging software or AI tool that civil engineers are beginning to use.
Present all of your work in a concise, 6-slide portfolio that shows your new skills.
Spreadsheet proficiency: comfortable entering quantities, using simple formulas, and drawing quick Gantt bars in Google Sheets or Excel.
Basic scheduling concepts: understand that tasks have durations and depend on each other; we'll build a simple schedule together.
Plan-reading basics: recognize symbols/line types on a civil plan sheet; we'll decode a sample in class.
Permitting awareness: know that projects require ROW, environmental, and agency permits; we'll map the key approvals.
Project execution mindset: willingness to track progress, flag issues, and communicate clearly in a team setting.

projects.title: Aspiring Entrepreneur: Build Your First Business Plan

content.text: Create a step-by-step business plan while learning essential strategies in market research, marketing, operations, and financial planning to launch your own venture.

Small businesses and startups form the backbone of the global economy, but many fail within the first few years due to a lack of proper planning and strategy. In this Build Project, you'll step into the shoes of an aspiring entrepreneur and develop a comprehensive business plan, addressing the key challenges businesses face, such as understanding their market, crafting effective strategies, and managing finances. Under the guidance of an experienced industry professional, you'll conduct market research, create a value proposition, plan operations, design marketing strategies, and estimate financial projections. This project will expose you to fundamental business methodologies and tools, simulating the responsibilities of real-world business managers and entrepreneurs.
By the end of the project, you will be able to:
Develop a comprehensive business plan including market research, marketing strategies, operations, and financial projections.
Identify and analyze a target market, including competitors and customer needs.
Craft a unique value proposition that differentiates your business from competitors.
Create a basic financial forecast, including costs, revenues, and profit estimates.
Present a business idea effectively, using clear communication and structured storytelling techniques.
For you to be successful in this project, you will need:

Proficiency in presentation tools: Familiarity with software like PowerPoint, Google Slides, or Canva to create and deliver a slide deck.

projects.title: AI-Powered Industrial Quality Control: Build a Visual Defect Detection System

content.text: Build an end-to-end machine vision system that automatically detects surface defects in manufacturing environments using deep learning and computer vision techniques.

Automated quality control is essential in manufacturing, automotive, electronics, and other industries, enabling real-time, high-precision inspection of products at scale using intelligent machine vision systems. By replacing or augmenting manual inspection with AI-powered defect detection, manufacturers can ensure uniform quality standards, detect minute surface anomalies, and reduce human error—especially in high-throughput environments.

In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Machine Vision Engineer and develop a complete automated visual inspection system that mimics real-world manufacturing quality control processes. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll learn how industrial cameras work, process defect datasets, train convolutional neural networks for defect classification, and deploy your model through an interactive web application. You'll become familiar with industry tools like PyTorch and techniques like transfer learning, model evaluation metrics, deployment frameworks like Streamlit, and DevOps practices including CI/CD pipelines. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real machine vision engineering team.
Understand how industrial camera systems capture and process images for automated quality inspection
Build and train deep learning models for visual defect detection using transfer learning with PyTorch
Deploy trained models through web interfaces for real-time inference and visualization
Implement automated testing and continuous integration pipelines using GitHub Actions
Create professional project documentation and present technical work effectively

Python programming experience: You should be comfortable writing functions, working with classes, and using libraries like NumPy and Pandas. This is essential for implementing data processing pipelines, training loops, and building the web application.

Basic command line usage: You need to know how to navigate directories (cd, ls), run Python scripts, and use basic Git commands (clone, commit, push). These skills are necessary for managing your project repository and running code.

Familiarity with installing Python packages: You should be able to use pip or similar package managers to install libraries and manage dependencies. This is needed to set up your development environment with PyTorch, Streamlit, and other tools.

Completed at least one Python programming course: Whether through coursework like CS101 or self-study, you should have foundational programming knowledge. This ensures you can follow along with code examples and implement solutions independently.
No prior machine learning or deep learning experience required: All computer vision and ML concepts will be taught from the ground up with hands-on examples, so beginners in AI are welcome.

projects.title: Building an Ideal Customer Profile through Market Data Analysis

content.text: Develop a data-driven Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) by analyzing customer, market, and performance data to inform B2B SaaS go-to-market strategy.

Every software company lives or dies by one question: who are our best customers, and how do we find more of them? In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Market Research Analyst at a B2B SaaS company and dig into real-world-style data to answer it. Working from a prebuilt customer dataset we provide, and under the guidance of an experienced industry professional, you'll spot patterns across industries, company sizes, and buying behaviors, build a segmentation model, and define an Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) that pinpoints exactly who the business should target. You'll do all of your analysis in familiar, free tools like Excel or Google Sheets, in an environment that simulates how a real SaaS go-to-market team operates.
Analyze structured datasets to identify high-value customer segments

Evaluate segment performance using metrics such as conversion rates, deal size, and win rates

projects.title: Building Engaging Compliance Training: Developing an Interactive Quiz for Regulatory Awareness

content.text: This project focuses on developing a learning material to help employees understand and comply with key workplace regulations, including anti-harassment policies, data protection, and workplace safety.

With workplace regulations increasingly under scrutiny, organizations are prioritizing compliance to protect both employees and the business. Understanding and adhering to policies around anti-harassment, data privacy, and safety are now essential components of a healthy workplace culture. This Build Project will guide you through the process of designing a compliance training tool, focusing on creating an interactive quiz that reinforces knowledge about critical workplace regulations such as anti-harassment policies, data privacy laws (e.g., GDPR), and safety standards.

Over the course of 8 weeks, you will work on developing content, building quiz questions, and incorporating learning design strategies to ensure the material is engaging and easy to retain. By the end of the project, you’ll gain practical experience in both compliance and training development, equipping you with skills to build effective, engaging learning materials that foster a safer and more compliant workplace.

By the end of the 8-weeks project, you will develop an interactive compliance quiz. The quiz will be designed to be completed by employees in a corporate setting and will reinforce understanding of key regulations.
Develop a compliance quiz that assesses employees' understanding of key regulations, such as anti-harassment and data protection.
Learn how to create engaging and accessible learning materials to promote compliance in the workplace.
Understand the psychology behind how people learn and retain compliance-related information.
Gain experience designing and delivering training modules with tangible outcomes.

Interest in Learning Design and Employee Training: You should have a foundational understanding of employee training principles, such as learner engagement and information retention. An interest in making complex topics accessible and engaging will be crucial for developing effective educational tools in this project.

Basic Knowledge of Workplace Compliance Topics: Familiarity with compliance issues, including anti-harassment policies, data privacy laws (e.g., GDPR), and workplace safety, will help you craft accurate, relevant quiz content that aligns with real-world standards.

Prior Experience with Training Content Creation: Previous exposure to designing or delivering training materials, such as creating presentation slides, writing quiz questions, or facilitating workshops, will aid you in developing engaging and understandable quiz content.

Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills: You should be able to critically evaluate complex legal concepts and translate them into clear, practical quiz questions. The ability to create realistic scenarios or cases for compliance training will also be beneficial.

projects.title: Building Legal Cases for Human Rights

content.text: Investigate real-world human rights violations and simulate litigation before regional human rights bodies, developing legal arguments, briefs, and advocacy skills throughout the process.

Human rights violations across the Americas continue to challenge governments, courts, and civil society. Understanding how to analyze these violations through regional legal frameworks and advocate effectively before international bodies is a critical skill for aspiring legal professionals and policy advocates. In this Build Project, you’ll wear the hat of a Human Rights Legal Advocate and develop a full legal case based on real-world violations, simulating proceedings before the Inter-American Commission or Court of Human Rights. Under the supervision of an experienced legal professional, you’ll examine facts, identify applicable legal norms, and conduct legal research on relevant treaties, jurisprudence, and comparative frameworks to build strong legal arguments. You’ll become familiar with tools and methodologies such as treaty interpretation, jurisprudential analysis, comparative legal reasoning, international legal writing skills, and oral advocacy strategy. All of this will take place in a collaborative environment that simulates the workflow of an international litigation and advocacy team.1b:T64
Understand the foundations of public international law and international human rights law, including key treaties, institutions, and enforcement mechanisms.
Distinguish between universal and regional human rights systems, with a focus on the Inter-American Human Rights System.
Analyze human rights cases from the Inter-American Commission and Court, applying relevant legal norms and precedents.
Apply legal research techniques to identify relevant norms, precedents, and institutional mechanisms for regional accountability.

Draft legal advocacy documents — including a legal mapping worksheet, case brief, and written legal argument — consistent with the procedures and standards of the Inter-American Commission and Court of Human Rights.
An interest in international human rights litigation or legal advocacy.
Comfort reading and processing complex, text-heavy materials, such as reports, decisions, or institutional documents.
Basic writing and communication skills, with a willingness to develop legal argumentation in both written and oral form.
Analytical thinking and logical reasoning, especially when working with case-based scenarios.
Strong reading comprehension and attention to detail.

projects.title: Building & Scaling a Youth Sports Club

Develop a comprehensive business plan, including financial projections and operational strategies.

Articulate a vision for growth and sustainability, demonstrating the social impact of their venture.

projects.title: Business Strategy 101: From Idea to Execution

content.text: Learn the building blocks of business strategy: market research, financial analysis, and strategic planning.

Most new ventures fail not because of bad ideas, but because founders lack the skills to test, plan, and execute them. Having a great idea is one thing but knowing how to turn it into a real business is another. This project teaches you how to do that.

In this Build Project, you will wear the hat of a Founder, as you develop and plan your own business or social enterprise. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you will how learn to research whether your idea can work, build a financial plan, and develop a strategy to bring your idea to market. You will become familiar with frameworks like the Business Model Canvas and SWOT analysis, conduct market research, and use Excel for financial modeling and Google Slides or Canva for pitch design. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real startup team. By the end, you'll have the foundational skills that apply to entrepreneurship, consulting, corporate strategy, or any role where you need to think critically about how businesses work.
Research and analyze a market: Learn how to assess whether a business idea has potential by researching customers, competitors, and market size.
Understand the financial side of a business: Learn how to project revenue and costs and understand key metrics that determine whether a business can sustain itself.
Design a business model: Learn how to map out how a business creates value, reaches customers, and makes money using the Business Model Canvas.
Think strategically about competition: Learn how to identify what makes a business stand out and how to plan for entering a market.
Communicate your ideas clearly: Learn how to present a business concept in a clear, persuasive pitch, whether in writing or presentation form.
Basic understanding of business concepts (revenue, costs, profit)
Ability to research markets online and interpret basic data (trends, competitors, customer insights)
Familiarity with presentation tools such as software like PowerPoint, Google Slides, or Canva to create and deliver a slide deck.
Ability to communicate ideas clearly in writing and presentations

projects.title: C++ Systems for Finance: Build a Trading Exchange from Scratch

content.text: Develop a C++ trading system that combines software engineering expertise with financial market knowledge.

As financial markets become more digitalized globally, there is increasing demand for developments in systematic trading. In this Build project, you’ll wear the hat of a software developer and build a live trading exchange. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you’ll be writing C++ to develop this exchange that includes an order gateway and a matching engine with an order book. You’ll become familiar with best practices to write latency-aware C++, which will prepare you for entry-level roles at a quantitative trading firm.
Design and implement production-ready C++ systems following sound software engineering principles
Analyze and model the design and interactions among exchange components
Evaluate and compare tradeoffs between alternative data structures
Measure, benchmark, and optimize code for performance and efficiency
Experience with object‑oriented programming, including writing programs that use loops, conditionals, functions, and classes.
Familiarity with common data structures such as vectors, maps, and heaps, and an understanding of when each is appropriate.
A foundational understanding of computer systems, including networking concepts, basic multithreading, and synchronization (e.g., locks or mutexes).
Comfort using the terminal and Git, including navigating directories, running commands, and managing code with Git/GitHub.
Exposure to modern C++ features and the C++ standard library (not required, but a strong plus for an advanced project).

fellows.name: Yiwen Victor Song

projects.title: Cash Flow in Action: Stablize a Distressed Company by Financial Restructuring

content.text: Build a dynamic, 13-week cash flow forecast that diagnoses a business crisis and guides strategic restructuring decisions for a financially distressed company in any industry.

This Build Project puts you in the driver’s seat of financial restructuring. You’ll step into a small-to-medium-sized distressed company in the U.S. - playing the roles of restructuring analysts, project managers, and even interim CEOs. You will investigate the root causes of distress, test alternative scenarios, and recommend restructuring solutions while learning how to communicate complex information clearly and professionally to creditors, investors, and other key stakeholders. Along the way, you will develop critical skills in financial analysis, scenario modeling, and strategic decision-making, gaining hands-on experience that mirrors the genuine challenges faced by professionals in private equity, corporate finance, restructuring advisory, and financial operations - skills that are highly sought after in today’s U.S. workforce.
Conduct a situational assessment of a distressed company - including operational, strategic, and financial analysis - and recommend the most appropriate restructuring remedy
Communicate case-administration updates clearly and sensitively to various stakeholders (creditors, investors, management) in the form of presentation decks
Summarize large amounts of data into presentations for secured creditors and potential buyers
Perform a high-level valuation analysis to inform restructuring options
Build a 13-week (quarterly) cash flow forecast to demonstrate stabilization and forward-looking planning

Familiarity with the three core financial statements -  Income Statement, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow Statement - and an introductory understanding of how they relate to a company’s financial position
Working knowledge of financial concepts such as cash flow management, valuation analysis, and drivers of financial distress.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including the use of basic formulas and scenario modeling for financial analysis and forecasting

Proficiency in Microsoft Powerpoint and a willingness to explore effective communication and presentation strategies for summarizing complex financial and operational information for creditors, investors, and other stakeholders
Willingness to explore legal and stakeholder considerations in receivership, bankruptcy, and restructuring, and apply professional judgment in sensitive communication

projects.title: Climate Data Analysis & Visualization with Python

content.text: Analyze and visualize real-world climate data using Python to uncover trends in global temperature and CO₂ levels, creating a professional climate data report.

Data science plays a crucial role in understanding climate change, allowing scientists and policymakers to analyze trends, make predictions, and develop solutions. This project introduces you to the fundamentals of climate data analysis using Python, focusing on real-world datasets from NASA and NOAA.

In this Build Project, you will step into the role of a Data Scientist working in the environmental sector. You will learn how to access, clean, and analyze climate data, create compelling visualizations, and interpret key indicators such as global temperature rise and CO₂ levels. The project is designed to be accessible to students with basic Python knowledge, focusing on step-by-step learning and practical implementation. By the end, you will have a structured portfolio piece, showcasing your ability to analyze and communicate climate data effectively.
Use Python to load, clean, and analyze real-world climate datasets from NASA and NOAA.
Create effective data visualizations (graphs, heatmaps, and trend analysis) using Matplotlib and Seaborn.
Interpret and identify long-term climate trends from historical data.
Present findings in a clear and professional format, using Jupyter Notebooks, GitHub, and slide decks.
Gain insight into climate data science and its role in environmental decision-making.
Basic Python knowledge: ability to use loops, functions, and Pandas for data manipulation.
Introductory knowledge of data visualization: basic experience with Matplotlib or Seaborn is helpful.
Basic understanding of climate science concepts (helpful but not required).

projects.title: Cloud Data Pipeline for Dental Patient Data

content.text: Develop a scalable cloud Data Pipeline to Analyze Health Records.

Develop a scalable cloud Data Pipeline to Analyze Health Records using python as main tech stack. In the meantime, utilizing Google cloud project to setup a data intensive and scalable cloud infrastructure.
Python.
Cloud infrastructure deployment.
Rest development.
Basic knowledge of Python: you should be able to understand, modify and enhance given python source code.
Other prerequisites: Before the project starts,
You'll need to set up a Google Collab/local python env, GitHub, and Google Cloud accounts.

projects.title: Code & Cooking: Build a Meal Finder App

content.text: Go from a blank screen to a live meal finder app you can share and see how a real web app gets built and shipped in just 8 weeks.

Software isn’t just about writing code: it’s planning, building in small steps, and making sure what you built works for real people. In this project, you’ll build a meal-finder web app that suggests meal ideas based on your input. You’ll practice how teams work day-to-day by turning a request into a clear plan, building features step by step, and improving the app based on what you learn. You’ll also learn the basics of working with real data, handling common edge cases, and adding simple checks, so changes don’t break the main flow. By the end, you’ll have a live app you can share and a clear walkthrough of how you built it.
Describe how a software team moves work from idea to release, including roles, ceremonies, and day-to-day communication.
Use React to break down a UI into reusable and functional components and use Tailwind CSS to style and layout the application.
Explore and navigate a real codebase, understanding how pages, components, and data flow connect to each other.
Implement a connection to an external API and identify how data moves from a server response to what a user sees on screen.
Recognize the role of automated testing, continuous integration, and deployment in the software release process, from catching bugs to getting an app live.

Know how to build and style a web page with HTML and CSS: you can create a basic page structure with elements like headings, buttons, and forms, and use CSS to control how they look. You do not need to be an expert, but you should not be seeing HTML or CSS for the first time.
Write basic JavaScript: you have used variables, functions, and conditionals before and can follow along when someone explains what a piece of code does.
Use Git and GitHub at a basic level: you can clone a repository, make a commit, and push changes.
Run a project from the terminal: you can open a terminal, navigate to a folder, and run commands like npm install and npm run dev.

projects.title: Code To Execution: Build Your Own Interpreter

content.text: Build a simple interpreter step-by-step and discover how computers run your code using trees, recursion, and real software engineering concepts.

Programming languages are at the core of almost every software system and understanding how code is executed is a fundamental skill for entry-level software engineers. In this Build Project, you'll step into the role of a software engineer and build a simple interpreter that reads and executes a small programming language. Under guidance, you'll implement key components such as expression evaluation and tree-based program representation using a provided code framework. You'll become familiar with concepts and techniques such as recursion, Abstract Syntax Trees, and program execution. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the work of a real software engineering team building developer tools.
Represent programs using tree structures (Abstract Syntax Trees)
Evaluate expressions in a programming language using recursion
Implement the core components of a basic interpreter for a simple language
Extend your language by adding new syntax or language features
Introductory programming experience – you should be comfortable writing simple programs in Python, Java, JavaScript, or another programming language.
Understanding of basic programming concepts – you should know how to use variables, functions, conditional statements, and loops.
Ability to read and modify existing code – during the project you will work with and extend code provided in the sessions.

fellows.name: Yuwei Ye

projects.title: Valuing a Global Company: Create a Professional Equity Investment Memo

content.text: Gain hands-on experience assessing growth, returns, capital allocation, and valuation as you evaluate investment opportunities in international public equities and practice financial modeling.

In this Build Project, you’ll learn how investors decide to invest in a business deemed to provide a compelling future return. Through the 8-week project, you will act and think like an investment analyst, including conducting your own due diligence on a potential new investment idea. Under the guidance of an experienced industry expert, you will identify, assess and evaluate a potential investment opportunity, analyze the company’s performance, and build an Excel financial model to value it. You will summarize and present your research in an investment recommendation in PowerPoint, honing all-important skills for entry-level roles across Finance, Accounting, Banking, Investment Management, and Consulting industries.

Identify, assess, and analyze sources of corporate competitive advantage in potential equity investments, including their connection to key financial metrics that investors use to evaluate businesses.
Build financial models in Microsoft Excel to help value businesses and potential equity investments.
Prepare and present an investment recommendation for a potential equity investment.
A basic understanding of accounting principles (e.g., revenue, cost of goods sold, profits) and finance concepts (e.g., equity, debt)
Past experience using Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets (experience performing basic sums, products, etc.)
An interest in financial markets, and a desire to develop the “investor toolkit” and learn how professional investors evaluate investment opportunities
Strong oral and written communication skills, with a desire to discuss, debate, and share your thoughts with others

projects.title: Conduct an Enterprise Valuation Analysis for a Potential Acquisition

content.text: Conduct an enterprise valuation analysis for a growing tech company using Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) and multiples analyses to assess its value in a potential acquisition.

In this project, you will step into the role of a finance professional evaluating a growing software company in the context of a potential acquisition. Working with real-world-style financial information, you will explore the company’s historical performance, develop a view of its future financial potential, and assess what the business could be worth using different valuation approaches. Along the way, you will experience how finance professionals combine financial analysis, market data, and professional judgment to develop a valuation range and support an acquisition decision.
Develop a financial forecast for a growing software company and identify the key business drivers that influence future performance.
Explain and apply the fundamentals of Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation, including how key assumptions and sensitivities impact enterprise value.
Apply Comparable Company (Trading Multiples) and Precedent Transaction (Transaction Multiples) analyses to assess a company’s value relative to the market.
Compare and interpret different valuation methodologies to develop a defensible enterprise valuation range and support a potential acquisition decision.
Clearly communicate financial analysis and valuation conclusions through a finance industry-standard presentation.
Basic Excel skills, including entering data, using simple formulas, and working with tables.
Basic understanding of financial statements, including the purpose of an income statement and common concepts such as revenue, expenses, and profit.
Basic numerical and analytical skills, including working with percentages, growth rates, and simple calculations.
Ability to interpret data and identify trends in financial or business information.
No prior valuation or M&A experience is required.

projects.title: Conducting, Crafting and Analyzing Impactful Email Campaigns

content.text: Understand the fundamental aspects of digital marketing and CRM, design an email campaign based on a pre-established strategy and evaluate key performance indicators.

Join a hands-on project exploring the dynamic world of digital marketing and Customer Relationship Management (CRM).
In this Build Project, you'll develop essential CRM skills such as managing customer data and building meaningful customer relationships. You'll create your own email marketing campaign aligned with specific marketing goals and learn how to evaluate its success using key performance indicators (KPIs).

You'll also gain practical experience in:

Segmenting your audience to deliver targeted messages,
Personalizing content to boost engagement,
Running A/B tests to identify the most effective campaign strategies.

These in-demand skills are highly valuable for entry-level roles in marketing and CRM, helping you stand out in a competitive job market and contribute to companies focused on customer engagement and retention.
Gain hands-on experience with CRM practices: Learn how to effectively manage customer data and interactions.
Understand audience segmentation and personalization: Use customer data to tailor email content and increase engagement rates.
Track and interpret key performance indicators (KPIs): Measure the effectiveness of email marketing and CRM efforts.
Conduct A/B tests on email campaigns: Test subject lines, content, and strategies to optimize campaign performance and refine marketing approaches over time.
Basic Marketing Concepts: Understand core concepts like segmentation, KPIs, and email campaigns.

Strategic Thinking: Design email campaigns that align with business goals and are tailored to specific customer personas. Ensure your emails contribute to the broader marketing objectives of the company.
Data Analysis Skills: Analyze campaign data (e.g., open rates, click-through rates, conversion rates) to make data-driven decisions that enhance campaign effectiveness and drive better results.

Copywriting Excellence: Write compelling and persuasive email content that clearly communicates the message, encourages desired actions (like clicks or purchases), and stays consistent with the brand’s voice and style.
Visual Design Skills: Create visually appealing email templates, graphics, and layouts using tools like Canva or InDesign to capture the reader's attention and improve engagement.

projects.title: Think Like a Buy‑Side Analyst: Research & Pitch Global Hardware Stocks

content.text: Break down tech hardware companies, spot growth trends, and build simple forecasts using Excel and Bloomberg resulting in a pitch-deck ready strategy.

The stock market is always changing rapidly, especially in the hardware sector. Thus, spotting your own advantages and finding the right trend is so important. In this Build Projects, you’ll imagine you are an entry level buy-side analyst and develop your own investment ideas. During the process, you will get to know how the hardware supply chain works. You will be able to create and conduct your own investment strategy in the technology stock market.

Learning how to filter the right trends and right companies in the hardware and technology industry, it will help you to narrow down and focus on the appropriate investment targets. To make a high conviction investment idea, it is important to conduct further fundamental research among the supply chains and make your own financial forecast compared to industry peers. You will become familiar with excel and Bloomberg. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real investment team.
Enhance the investment sense and filter out the growing market trends.
Build research methods and investment strategies.
Make judgements and forecasts based on qualitative and quantitative research.
Conduct a write-up and make a presentation deck for idea pitch.
Basic understanding of financial statements, including income statement, cash flow statement, and balance sheet.
Basic understanding of the hardware industry, including memory, foundry, optical fiber/cable, assembly makers, GPU/CPU, and IC design houses.
Basic skills in Excel and PowerPoint.
Passion for fundamental research and the stock market.
