projects.title: Construct a Pro Forma Financial Model for a Software Startup

content.text: Forecast and model the financial performance of a high-growth startup.

The ability to deconstruct and forecast the growth and quality of a business is foundational to a career in finance and investing. In this Build Project, you will mimic the work of a financial analyst and create a financial model that forecasts the trajectory of an early-stage software startup. Alongside your project leader, you will build a 3-statement financial model that showcases future financial performance based on present and past business assumptions. You will familiarize yourself with software-specific accounting concepts like deferred revenue and accumulated deficit as well as spreadsheet modeling standards and techniques — all of which are skills used and valued by real finance teams.
How to build a 3-statement financial forecast of an early-stage startup using MS Excel or Google Sheets.
How to utilize accounting concepts like deferred revenue and retained earnings as well as software-specific concepts like net revenue retention and annual contract value.
How to use MS Excel or Google Sheets formulas like INDEX/MATCH and SUMIFS/COUNTIFS and techniques like formula-fills and cell references.
Commitment to start and finish the project, actively participate in all meetings, and work independently for ~1 hour/week.
Basic knowledge of accounting: you should be able to distinguish between the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement.
Basic knowledge of MS Excel/Google Sheets: you should have an understanding of most ribbon functionality and basic formulas and shortcuts.

projects.title: Control a Robot's Navigation Through a Warehouse

content.text: Use Python to plan and control paths for an autonomous mobile robot used to unload containers in a warehouse.

Increasing efficiency of robot movements is a constant battle that people in Mechatronics are fighting daily. In this Build Project, you’ll wear the hat of Robotics Mechatronics Engineer and enable a robot to navigate autonomously at dock doors in a simulated warehouse. Under the supervision of an experienced Build Fellow, you'll use Python to implement trajectories planning and following algorithms to allow an autonomous mobile robot to navigate. You’ll become familiar with the state-of-the-art ROS2 (Robot Operating System 2) and testing in simulation. The implemented solution will reflect current industry best practices.
Leverage ROS2 to implement a multi-process navigation system.
Implement a basic 2D path planner.
How to generate a time-parametrized trajectory from a 2D Path.
Implement a controller allowing the mobile robots to track a trajectory.
Visualize your results using the gazebo simulator and rviz2.
Commitment to start and finish the project, actively participate in all meetings, and work independently for ~2 hour/week.
Curiosity, willingness to learn, and proactive communication.

Intermediate knowledge of Python for scientific computing: you should have already contributed to a project with multiple files (i.e. be used to importing objects from other packages, modules or files), you should be able to use NumPy to perform array operations
Having taken an introductory class covering either robotics, control theory, mechanics or physics: you should be comfortable with the notion of derivatives (especially time derivatives)
Being comfortable with 2D geometry and the notion of frame: you should be comfortable using trigonometry in 2D

Interest in robotics and autonomous navigation, being keen to dive into the complexity of robotics software systems, being interested in working with complex industrial-grade solutions such as ROS2 and docker.

projects.title: Create a Personalized AI Chatbot That Talks to Your Data

content.text: Design and build a smart AI chatbot that can interact with your private data, using advanced retrieval-augmented generation techniques.

In the tech industry, AI-driven solutions are becoming increasingly essential, with chatbots playing a crucial role in automating customer support, data retrieval, and personalized assistance across various sectors. In this Build Project, you will design and build an intelligent local AI chatbot that can understand and interact with your personal data using cutting-edge Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques. You will learn how to preprocess and index private data, integrate advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) models, and work with industry-standard tools. Through hands-on experience, you will gain the skills needed to create scalable, efficient AI systems that solve real-world challenges. By mastering these skills, you’ll be well-equipped for in-demand entry-level roles such as AI Developer, Data Analyst, or NLP Engineer, positioning you to thrive in today’s rapidly evolving tech industry.

Design and implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures, combining state-of-the-art retrieval techniques with generative AI models to generate contextually relevant and accurate responses.
Utilize cutting-edge tools such as LangChain, OpenAI’s GPT, and vector databases to build advanced conversational AI systems that interact seamlessly with your data.

Master techniques for processing and querying large datasets, including algorithms for splitting, indexing, and retrieving information from large documents or extensive knowledge repositories to optimize chatbot performances.
Intermediate skills of programming in python: You should be able to write functions, classes, class attributes, for loops, if statements, break statements)

Foundational Knowledge of NumPy: You should understand array shapes and how to manipulate them (reshaping, slicing, indexing). You should also be comfortable performing vectorized operations and basic matrix operations.
Basic Mathematical Concepts: A clear understanding of vector representations, including how embeddings work in a vector space.

fellows.name: Denis Lusson

projects.title: Create a Strengths-Based Company Culture

content.text: Explore strategies for identifying employees’ strengths and integrating them into their roles to foster a strengths-based company culture.

By the end of the 8-week project, students will develop a comprehensive 'How-to Guide' for creating and sustaining a strengths-based company culture, based on their experiences with personality tests and talent management practices. A template will be provided to guide them through the process. Throughout the project, students will engage in various activities including analyzing personality tests, identifying individual strengths, and applying talent management practices. Key deliverables will include a strengths assessment, an implementation plan for fostering a strengths-based culture, and regular reflections on their learning process.
Design personalized development plans tailored to maximize employee potential and job satisfaction.
Develop strategies to integrate strengths into employees’ roles effectively.
Implement techniques to foster a strengths-based company culture.
Analyze real-world examples of strengths-based cultures and apply lessons learned.
Get to know a variety of personality tests.
Self-Reflection to identify personal and professional goals, strengths, and areas for development.
Analytic Thinking to analyze personality tests and performance evaluations.
Creativity to think outside the box and generate original ideas for organizational culture.
Communication Skills to articulate strengths and design effective development plans.
Time Management to balance the project workload and meet deadlines.

fellows.name: Silvia Schweinoester

projects.title: Behind the Panels: ACM Shop Drawings

content.text: Learn the step-by-step process of creating ACM (Aluminum Composite Material) shop drawings as the foundation for panel fabrication using AutoCAD.
The complexity of material usage is a major challenge in the architecture, engineering, and construction industry, and the ability to address it is a key professional skill.

In this Build Project, you will develop shop drawings for the ACM (Aluminum Composite Material) scope of work and learn how panels are detailed. projects.title: Data Detective: Catching Trade Errors

content.text: Build automated tools to extract, clean, and reconcile stock trading data using SQL and Python, just like analysts in a real-world trading firm.

Every trade made on Wall Street creates a wave of data that must be tracked, cleaned, verified, and reported. This work is at the heart of many entry level positions in trading firms, investment banks, and fintech companies. In this Build Project you will step into the role of a junior operations analyst and work with public stock market data to extract, clean, reconcile, and visualize trading activity.

Guided by an experienced industry professional, you will simulate transaction records, write SQL queries, create automated Python reports, and detect inconsistencies in the data that mirror the reconciliation work done in real operations teams. You will gain hands on experience with essential tools such as SQL, Python with Pandas and Matplotlib, and reconciliation logic, all in a simulated environment that reflects the workflows of modern financial data teams.
Query and extract financial market data using SQL
Clean and validate large datasets using Python and Pandas
Automate daily financial reports using simple Python scripts
Reconcile simulated trade and position data to detect errors
Visualize financial data and operational insights using Matplotlib or Seaborn

Basic SQL skills: you should be able to write simple SELECT, WHERE, and JOIN queries to pull specific data from a table. If you’ve done a class project or lab involving database queries, you’re ready.

Basic Python skills: you should be comfortable opening a dataset in Pandas, viewing and filtering data, and performing simple calculations. If you’ve used Python in a data analysis course or for a small personal project, that’s enough.
Some first exposure to data visualization: you should know how to create basic charts in Matplotlib or Seaborn (bar charts, line graphs) and label them clearly.
Attention to detail: reconciliation work requires noticing when numbers don’t match, so you should be comfortable double-checking results and thinking through why data might be inconsistent.
Curiosity about finance or data workflows: you do not need prior finance experience, but you should enjoy working with datasets, spotting patterns, and solving small data “mysteries.”

projects.title: Think Like a Fund Manager: Data‑Driven Asset Allocation in Python

content.text: Work hands‑on with market returns to compare portfolio approaches, validate results against benchmarks like the S&P 500, and communicate conclusions through a presentation and Jupyter notebook analysis.

Asset allocation is a foundational task in investment management and a core responsibility in entry-level roles across asset management, hedge funds, and quantitative finance teams. In this project, you will take on the role of a fund manager and design their own asset allocation strategy using real-world financial data. Under the guidance of an experienced finance professional, you will learn to formulate investment problems, apply quantitative models such as mean-variance optimization and factor-based approaches, and implement strategies using Python. Through rigorous backtesting and benchmarking against market benchmarks like the S&P 500, you will assess performance, robustness, and practical viability. This hands-on experience will not only deepen you understanding of financial theory but also equip you with in-demand skills in data analysis, portfolio construction, and risk evaluation—key capabilities for launching a career in investment research, portfolio analytics, or quantitative finance.
Formulate real-world asset allocation problems and understand the intuition behind various investment criteria (e.g., risk-return tradeoff).
Solve classical and modern portfolio optimization models (e.g., mean-variance) using Python and numerical techniques.
Conduct robust backtesting of asset allocation strategies with real market data and compare them to standard benchmarks like equal-weight and market portfolios.
Interpret strategy performance using financial metrics (e.g., Sharpe ratio) and evaluate robustness across different market regimes.
Develop data-driven insights and clearly communicate the rationale and results of asset allocation decisions, bridging theory with investment practice.

projects.title: Design Your Own Range-Extended Electric Vehicle Concept

content.text: Step into the role of an entry-level electrical engineer as you explore how range-extended electric vehicles work and create an original REEV concept for a real-world mission.

In this Build Project, you will step into the role of an entry-level electrical engineer and learn how the major components of a REEV work together. You will explore energy flow during charging, electric driving, regenerative braking, and range-extender operation. You will then apply these fundamentals to create your own REEV concept for a real-world mission and add a signature energy feature such as V2L, V2H, V2V, or emergency power.

By completing this project, you will practice systems thinking, concept development, diagramming, and technical presentation—skills relevant to entry-level roles in electrical engineering, electric vehicles, energy systems, and mobility. projects.title: Designing Remote Solar Microgrid Systems

Solutions such as standalone power systems which utilize renewable energy sources like solar and wind, offer localized solutions that reduce reliance on centralized grid infrastructure.  

In this Build Project, you will step into the role of an electrical engineer and develop a tool to assist with preliminary sizing of the electrical equipment for a remote microgrid system. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you will develop an understanding of the requirements and considerations that apply to each of the major microgrid components, and you will create a Python script that aggregates those system requirements in order to recommend an appropriately sized microgrid system. All this will happen in an environment that exposes you to the decisions that electrical engineers have to make, and the thought processes that go into every decision.

projects.title: Develop a Comprehensive Strategy for the Optimization of Gear Manufacturing Process

content.text: Optimize gear manufacturing for high quality, cost efficiency, reduced lead times, and resource efficiency by enhancing material usage, process reliability, and latest manufacturing techniques.

Gear manufacturing is essential for producing high-precision components used in critical systems across industries like automotive, aerospace, and renewable energy. Gears play a key role in transmitting power efficiently, and optimizing gear manufacturing significantly impacts industries by improving product performance, reducing operational costs, and enhancing machinery efficiency.

This Build Project aims to optimize the gear manufacturing process, focusing on producing high-quality gears at competitive costs and lead times. It involves a detailed analysis of gear design, materials, cutting tools, and machine setup, with the goal of improving efficiency, reducing defects, and enhancing production consistency. By researching current technologies and manufacturing methods, you will develop an optimized process flow and validate key parameters to ensure minimal tool wear, high precision, and reduced downtime. Ultimately, the project will provide organization with a comprehensive, cost-effective strategy for manufacturing superior gears that meet the demands of evolving industrial sectors.
Gain a comprehensive understanding of gear manufacturing processes, including key parameters like material selection, machine setup, and cutting tools.
Develop expertise in optimizing manufacturing workflows to enhance quality, reduce costs, and shorten lead times.
Strengthen problem-solving, data analysis, and process validation skills by testing and refining different production variables.

projects.title: From Market Crashes to Risk Control: Design a Data-Driven Tail Hedging Strategy in Python

content.text: Step into the role of a financial engineer by studying volatility and drawdowns, testing protection ideas with historical index data, and producing a complete analysis notebook and final presentation supported by Pandas‑based analytics and charts.

Amid the complex and far-reaching impacts of global events, today's financial markets are marked by heightened volatility and uncertainty, making investment decisions increasingly challenging. In this environment, understanding tail risk—the potential for extreme losses found in the far left of the return distribution—and designing tail hedge strategies has become essential for mitigating severe market downturns. In this project, you'll step into the role of a Financial Engineer, exploring tail hedge strategies as effective tools for managing significant drawdown risks. Guided by an experienced Project Leader, you will design, implement, and evaluate the empirical performance of these strategies using over 15 years of historical index and option data. Beyond technical execution, you'll be expected to form your own perspective on how these strategies may behave in future market conditions and propose cost-efficient, data-driven recommendations for clients. projects.title: Find Your Business in Digitalized Manufacturing

content.text: Identify a business opportunity with digitalized manufacturing in your chosen industry, and develop it into a viable business model.

Digital manufacturing technologies encompass a broad range of tools and systems that are transforming manufacturing through digitization and connectivity. They are foundational to the smart factory and Industry 4.0, where real-time data, automation, and advanced analytics drive efficiency. However, despite their potential, digital manufacturing technologies face challenges in scalability and integration within traditional manufacturing environments. In this Build Project, you will act as a multi-disciplinary analyst, selecting a digital manufacturing technology (such as IoT, robotics, or digital twins) to explore its applications in a specific industry sector. Guided by expert Project Leaders, you will analyze technology-specific challenges and the unique demands of your chosen industry, identify key stakeholders who influence adoption, and create a business plan to support implementation. By the end of the project, you will present this plan, demonstrating the role of digital manufacturing in enhancing productivity and agility. This project will introduce various digital manufacturing technologies and tools, including industrial IoT platforms, simulation software, and AI. To keep it realistic and fun, you will do your study in an environment simulating the operations of a real, small-scale startup team.
Learn the operations of a certain industry. Analyze an industrial sector and identify the manufacturing methods and suppliers critical to it.
Learn how to estimate a market size and its dependence on company operations and selected manufacturing innovation.
Learn about the limitations of a digital manufacturing technology of your choice (e.g., Additive Manufacturing) and how they impact commercialization.

Learn preparation and delivery of concise and comprehensive pitch-style presentations, which will summarize business- and technology- related findings about a chosen manufacturing industry, manufacturing company, its suppliers, and key technologies that are used already or can be used in the future.
Some background knowledge about manufacturing allowing to distinguish the principles behind different production methods.
Knowledge (and curiosity) about recent technological trends. E.g., see the TIME 2024 list here: https://time.com/collection/best-inventions-2024/.
General knowledge in quantitative analysis of a subject matter, e.g., using Excel.
Familiarity with reviewing literature and presenting its analysis on slides.

projects.title: Spotting Opportunities: Build a Digital Manufacturing Startup

content.text: Map the competitive landscape in a digital manufacturing space, identify an unmet market need, and build it into a pitch deck with honest market sizing.

Digital manufacturing technologies, from IoT sensors and robotics to digital twins and AI-driven analytics, are reshaping how products are made. They promise efficiency, agility, and new business models, but adopting them is rarely straightforward: companies face integration challenges, unclear ROI, and shifting competitive dynamics.

In this project you will step into the role of an entrepreneur-analyst. You will choose a manufacturing sector, map its competitive landscape, and look for gaps: problems that existing players aren't solving or markets they aren't serving well. You will then identify a digital manufacturing technology that could fill one of those gaps, size the market honestly (TAM down to a realistic SOM), and test whether there is genuine product-market fit. The result is a pitch deck built on that research.

Map a chosen sector's competitive landscape: Identify the key players in a manufacturing sector you select, outline a rough supply-chain map (a few tiers up and down), and spot gaps that existing companies aren't addressing.

Size a market opportunity (TAM/SAM/SOM): Break down the total, serviceable, and obtainable market for your idea. A recurring theme of the course: be honest about what your SOM realistically looks like for an early-stage venture.

Evaluate a technology as a business enabler: Assess how a chosen digital manufacturing technology (e.g., additive manufacturing, IoT, digital twins) could fill that gap, what limits its adoption, and how those limits shape your realistic market.
Build and defend a business case: Develop a concise business plan covering value proposition, target customer, revenue model, and key risks.
Present your business case: Assemble a slide deck that walks through your sector research, market sizing, and business model, and present it in a short structured pitch.
Basic understanding of manufacturing industries. You can read about how a product gets made and follow the supply-chain logic (who supplies what to whom); no hands-on engineering experience required.
Curiosity about technology trends. You follow tech news or lists like the TIME 2025 and reason about why technology matters: https://time.com/collection/best-inventions-2025/.
Comfort with simple quantitative analysis. You can build basic calculations in Excel or Google Sheets (e.g., market-size estimates, cost comparisons).

Ability to research, filter, and synthesize. You can use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT), articles, and company websites to gather information, critically assess what you find, and present your understanding on slides with confidence in what you're saying.

projects.title: Driving Efficiency in Solar Cell Manufacturing through LEAN

content.text: LEAN Operational Excellence is a management philosophy aimed at maximizing customer value by eliminating waste and enhancing efficiency across all aspects of an organization.    In this project, you will analyze and optimize the solar cell manufacturing process, identify areas of waste, and implement LEAN principles to enhance efficiency and quality, gaining practical experience in applying LEAN methodologies to real-world manufacturing challenges.

Lean Operational Excellence methodologies focus on identifying and eliminating waste in manufacturing processes, improving workflow efficiency, and enhancing overall productivity. These practices involve continuous improvement techniques such as Kaizen, 5S, and Value Stream Mapping to optimize every aspect of production. By implementing these methodologies, you can create a more streamlined, cost-effective, and high-quality manufacturing operation. Through the eight workshops, you will develop a comprehensive understanding of how to create both a value stream map and a future state value stream map. These sessions will provide you with a solid foundation in understanding the solar cell process flow, enabling you to identify inefficiencies and problems within the process. Additionally, you will learn how to design actionable improvement plans to enhance efficiency and value delivery. These workshops aim to equip you with the skills and knowledge needed for effective process optimization.
Learn how to streamline the processes and reduce waste, leading to higher productivity and efficiency in Solar Cell Fab.
Learn strategies to reduce costs by eliminating waste and optimizing the use of resources, thereby enhancing overall efficiency (Cost Minimization).
Develop strategies to identify and eliminate non-value-added activities, optimize workflow, and implement continuous improvement practices.
Basic Lean Principles: Understanding of Lean Manufacturing concepts, such as waste reduction, continuous improvement, and value creation.
Process Mapping: Familiarity with process mapping techniques and tools to visualize workflows and identify bottlenecks.
Data Analysis: Basic skills in data collection and analysis, including the ability to interpret metrics related to process performance.

projects.title: Drone Flight Planner System: Flight Path for Efficient Data Capture

content.text: Build a flight planner system which computes the trajectory for the drone to fly and capture photos efficiently as per user specification.

Capturing high quality image datasets is a rapidly expanding field with a wide range of applications: mapping, survey, digital 3D models, and datasets for AI. Drones are transforming the industry by providing a safe, cheap, and accessible platform which can navigate difficult terrain and capture datasets with remarkable precision and efficiency. In this project, you will wear the hat of a Roboticist and a Software Developer and develop a path planning system which can capture the image datasets in an efficient manner.

Under the guidance of an industry expert, you’ll develop data models in Python for user requirements and constraints, develop modular APIs to calculate the position and the speed of the drones, and build visualization tools to analyze the computed trajectories. You’ll learn about camera systems and the image capture process, mapping and photogrammetry concepts like overlap, and industry conventions to represent the path of robots. Your project leader will provide the mathematical concepts required for the project and simulate an environment of a real robotics software development team.
Learn fundamentals of camera systems, and model them in Python.
Understand the requirements of the image datasets captured by aerial photography.
Compute the positions and speed of the drone for photo captures.
Use Jupyter notebooks to share code, math, and visualizations in a modern and easy-to-follow medium.
Demonstrate the changes in the computed flight paths with modifications to the input specifications.
Basic knowledge of Python: basic syntax like loops, conditions, functions, and tools like unit testing, debugger.
Comfort with mathematical fundamentals like trigonometry.
Prior experience in mathematical frameworks like Numpy and Scipy is an added advantage. If not, they can easily be picked up alongside the project too.
Familiarity with Jupyter notebooks, and any plotting tools like Matplotlib/Plotly is a plus.

projects.title: Drug Development meets Physics

content.text: This project explores the applications of physics in drug development, enhancing our understanding and effectiveness of drugs from molecular interactions to delivery and quality control.

Spectroscopy and spectrometry are indispensable analytical techniques in drug discovery, extensively used to analyze molecular structures, interactions, and concentrations at every stage of the process. Their ability to provide detailed qualitative and quantitative data makes them essential for developing safe and effective drugs. In this Build Project, you will explore the physics principles behind these techniques and their real-world applications. You'll also read and analyze spectroscopy and spectrometry data. By the end of the project, you will be able to identify and present a real-life case study on their use in drug development. This project offers valuable, hands-on experience for students aiming for careers in biotechnology and drug development.

Gain skills in analyzing and interpreting spectroscopy and spectrometry data.
Use case studies and projects to apply what you've learned to real-world drug development scenarios.

projects.title: Build a Budget for an Early-Stage Startup

content.text: Learn how to build in Excel an operational and capital expenditure budget for a tech startup.

Wise financial planning is crucial for the success of any business; it becomes especially important for startups that have ambitious growth goals and limited resources. In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Financial Analyst and build a full-year budget that allows a fictional startup to understand its expenses and how much capital is needed to cover all business costs. You will create in Microsoft Excel a budget for employees’ salaries & benefits using dynamic formulas. Also, you’ll create a budget for professional service fees. Under the supervision of an experienced Build Fellow, you'll learn best practices in Financial Planning, specifics of operational and capital expenditure budgeting, and how to use Excel to create solid forecasting schedules. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real Financial Planning & Analysis team.
Design a Budget schedule for Overhead, Travel & Entertainment in Excel.

projects.title: Empowering Elementary Education Students to Emerge as Future Leaders

content.text: Develop purposeful integration between subject, pedagogical, and theoretical knowledge of a teacher to produce your own curriculum for personalized learning.

The aim of this Build Project is to discover methods to support curriculum development and teaching and learning best practices in any form and across all subject areas. You will learn to understand the importance of individualized and personalized learning, developmental goals, differentiation, cultural experiences and culturally responsive teaching, so that when you begin to work with children of all ages, gender and socio-economic backgrounds, you can effectively engage with and develop their love for learning with the idea they become lifelong learners.

Through correct pedagogy instruction and practice, you will develop your skills on how to support elementary students’ meta-cognitive skills and put this into practice in a classroom setting including the success criteria needed to do this. You will learn about, and adapt to, different methods of assessment so your students can acknowledge their own areas for improvement. You will learn about leadership in elementary schools and the experience and skills needed to progress into school leadership further on in your careers. Through guided instruction by an extremely experienced classroom teacher and school leader, you will know, use and apply micro-learning and asynchronous learning as well as write your own curriculum for personalized learning.

projects.title: Engineering the Space Grid: A Mission to Power Future Orbits

content.text: Apply aerospace engineering principles to design and simulate a CubeSat architecture that showcases advanced subsystem integration for precision orbital maneuvers.

Small satellites called CubeSats are used everywhere in the aerospace industry — from Earth imaging to deep space research — and their design requires engineers who can think across multiple systems. In this Build Project, you’ll step into the role of an Aerospace Systems Engineer to develop a CubeSat mission concept that can perform a simple orbital maneuver.

You’ll start by defining a clear mission objective, then build a system overview that shows how key subsystems like power, communications, and propulsion connect. Along the way, you’ll practice trade-off thinking (weight vs. power, orbit vs. propulsion) and reflect on how risks and reliability shape real missions.

Under the guidance of an industry mentor, you’ll use practical frameworks like Design for Manufacturing & Assembly (DFMA) and basic orbital math to make your design more realistic. The project will wrap up with a short team pitch, where you’ll showcase your CubeSat concept, walk through your design choices, and highlight lessons learned.
Define clear mission objectives by translating a broad space challenge into measurable system-level requirements.
Outline a CubeSat system architecture by identifying key subsystems (e.g., power, communications, propulsion) and explaining how they connect.
Apply basic aerospace engineering math by performing basic calculations and creating a power budget to assess mission feasibility.
Recognize risks and reliability factors by identifying potential failure modes and considering basic mitigation strategies.
Communicate engineering concepts effectively by presenting a concise summary of mission goals, design decisions, and lessons learned.
Foundations of Aerospace Engineering: Understanding of key aerospace concepts such as orbital mechanic, Kepler’s laws, Newtonian dynamics and spacecraft subsystem architecture

CAD Design and Mechanical Layout Skills: Experience with 3D modeling tools like Onshape, Solidworks, or CATIA, with an ability to interpret and manipulate assembly files related to space-grade mechanical components

Circuit and PCB Design Fundamentals: A basic knowledge of schematic capture and PCB layout using tools like KiCad or Eagle, including component placement, net routing, and generating Gerber/STEP files.

Numerical and Analytical Problem Solving: Awareness of how to derive engineering requirements from mission goals and how they drive architecture-level design. Exposure to methods like the V-model or MAHD is a plus.

Project Documentation and Engineering Communication: Ability to create structured documents (e.g., risk assessments, test plans, CAD drawings, subsystem charts) and present technical information clearly in both verbal and visual formats.

projects.title: Event Insight: Summarizing Disasters with AI and Web Data

content.text: Build an AI-powered 'situation brief' generator that combines real-time news analysis with web-sourced event images to help users understand the impact of natural disasters.

Natural disasters such as earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, and wildfires generate fast-moving, high-volume information that can be difficult for the public, emergency responders, and decision-makers to interpret quickly. In this Build Project, you will take on the role of a Data Scientist and develop a tool that helps summarize and visualize the impact of these events in a clear and accessible way.

You will build an application that takes a natural disaster query from the user and automatically creates a "situation brief" — a concise, structured report that combines insights from web-searched news content with relevant event images. To achieve this, you will first build an intent clarification agent that interacts with the user to resolve any ambiguity in their query (for example: which flood, which year, or which region). The refined query is then passed to an event identification agent that uses Gemini's built-in Google Search capability to retrieve current news articles and structured event details. A summarization agent then processes those articles to produce a clear, readable summary of the event.

Guided by a Data Science Fellow, you will learn how to connect multiple AI agents into a single workflow, how to validate and test each agent's inputs and outputs to ensure reliability. By the end of the project, you will have built a functional multi-agent application capable of generating a structured, data-driven situation brief for any natural disaster, helping users better understand its scale and impact.

projects.title: Fine-Tune a Job Title Embedding Model using Synthetic Training Data

content.text: Generate synthetic training data using an LLM API to fine-tune a SBERT-based embedding model to cluster similar job titles, evaluating the improvement in the embedding’s performance for retrieval.

Sentence embedding models have a wide variety of use cases in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) landscape, such as to facilitate vector search of unstructured text for semantically similar entries, or within a larger model to enable tasks such as regression or classification on free-text. During this project, you will devise a prompt to generate a synthetic dataset to fine-tune a pretrained sentence embedding model to address deficiencies in the domain-specific use-case of embedding job titles. You will then use this dataset to fine-tune your pretrained model and evaluate the improvement in performance for the vector search task. Finally, you will deploy your fine-tuned model within a Streamlit web app, allowing you to easily show your model to anyone. This project will help build your familiarity with basic prompting techniques, querying LLMs and parsing their outputs through an API, as well as popular Machine Learning and NLP frameworks (such as Hugging Face and Sentence-Transformers) and provide a compact end-to end experience from initial prototyping to dataset gathering, to training and evaluation, and finally deployment, covering the core parts of common workflows for a Data Scientist or ML Engineer.

Deploy a Streamlit web app to showcase a model and allow inference.

projects.title: From Plans to Quantities: Construction Project Estimating Essentials

content.text: Design an excel-based worksheet to estimate essential project materials such as concrete, CMU, and brick using real-life projects as a case study.

In the construction industry, accurate estimation of materials like concrete, steel, and brick is essential for project planning and budgeting. By designing a worksheet to estimate these materials, you will tackle a real-world challenge faced by construction companies daily. This project not only will give you practical skills crucial for success in the field but also fosters critical thinking, attention to detail, and problem-solving abilities essential for your professional development. Additionally, mastering estimation techniques enhances your employability and prepares you to contribute meaningfully to construction projects upon entering the workforce. In today's U.S. society, where infrastructure development and construction projects are essential for economic growth and societal well-being, professionals equipped with such skills play a vital role in driving progress and meeting the evolving needs of communities across the nation.
Understand and interpret the blueprints of a construction project.
Estimate concrete for a slab, steel for reinforcing and quantity of brick.
Build a report of the estimated materials.
Do a final presentation that is clear and concise.
Strong arithmetic skills, including the ability to perform calculations involving area, volume, and unit conversions.

Meticulous attention to detail. Students must carefully analyze project specifications, identify all relevant factors affecting material estimation, and avoid overlooking any crucial details that could lead to inaccuracies in their calculations.
Strong critical thinking skills to analyze complex problems, identify potential challenges in material estimation, and devise creative solutions.
Intermediate Excel level.

projects.title: From Raw Data to Strategic Decision-Making

content.text: Transform raw data into clean, meaningful insights through statistical analysis and predictive modeling.

Ever wonder how Netflix recommendations, hospital wait-time forecasts, or marketing A/B tests are constructed? They start with messy real-world data — and someone must turn that mess into answers. In this Build Project, you’ll step into the role of a junior data scientist and complete an end-to-end workflow you can proudly show on a resume. You’ll clean a raw dataset, explore patterns with visuals, spot and handle outliers, test a real hypothesis, and build predictive models.

You’ll work in Python notebooks using industry-standard tools (pandas, NumPy, visualization, basic statistical inference, Linear Regression, Random Forests, and model evaluation). Each week is broken into manageable tasks, with guidance from an experienced data science professional, so you build confidence while practicing how real analytics teams document decisions, compare models, and translate results into a clear, actionable story.
Clean and preprocess messy real-world datasets using Python, pandas, and NumPy.
Explore data and create useful visualizations with matplotlib and seaborn.
Use statistical inference to test simple hypotheses and explain uncertainty in practical terms.
Build and evaluate supervised learning models, including Linear Regression and Random Forests, with scikit-learn.
Communicate technical findings through a concise notebook, report, and final presentation.
Python programming: you should be comfortable writing variables, functions, loops, conditionals, and importing libraries.
Basic data handling: you should understand lists, dictionaries, tables, and the idea of rows and columns in a dataset.
Basic math and statistics: you should be familiar with mean, variance, distributions, correlation, and simple probability concepts.
Notebook workflow: you should be able to run code cells in Jupyter Notebook or a similar Python environment.
Visual interpretation: you should be comfortable reading basic charts such as histograms, scatterplots, and line plots.

projects.title: From Site to Strategy: Building Your First Commercial Real Estate Project

By the final week, you’ll deliver a professional-grade project pitch for a mock property, combining market insights, site feasibility, and basic financials.
Identify key differences between major commercial real estate asset classes (industrial, retail, office, mixed-use)
Conduct basic market and site analysis using publicly available data and mapping tools

An interest in real estate, business, or investment concepts
Willingness to research and interpret public data sources

projects.title: From Sketch to Factory: Heavy-Lift Drone Development

content.text: Develop a production-ready, high-strength, lightweight structural frame for a heavy-lift drone using parametric CAD workflows to automate design iterations, optimize for manufacturing (DFM), and ensure flight reliability.

Most modern high-tech devices, are far too complex and time-consuming to be designed or manufactured by a single individual. Luckily, the industry leverages the power of teamwork, where every engineer acts as a vital part of a larger, coordinated machine.

In this Build Project, you will step into the role of the Lead Mechanical Engineer within a simulated R&D team developing a heavy-lift autonomous delivery drone. While other specialized teams handle the flight electronics and software, you will own the structural integrity and manufacturing strategy of the Drone Arm Architecture.

The transition from conceptual 3D modeling to production-ready parts requires a deep understanding of parametric architecture, machine elements, material selection, and manufacturing constraints - skills that are essential across nearly all mechanical engineering specializations. In this professional environment, you will learn to justify your engineering decisions using simple calculations, tolerance stack-ups, and Design for Manufacturing (DFM) principles rather than "out-of-the-blue" modeling.

You will master industrial methodologies such as Top-Down Design in Fusion 360 and explore diverse manufacturing methods like additive manufacturing and CNC machining. This project environment is designed to simulate the operations of a real-world R&D lab, providing you with a safe space to ask questions, learn from mistakes, and build the confidence needed to thrive in a professional STEM workspace.
Build stable, fully parametric CAD models for a heavy-lift drone arm assembly, using key dimensions (such as propeller clearance and arm length) so the design can be updated easily without breaking.
Create and manage multiple design versions from a single CAD model to handle different payload requirements or use cases efficiently.

Support your design decisions using basic mechanical calculations (such as motor thrust loads, bolt shear strength, and propeller tip clearance) to ensure your parts are safe, functional, and manufacturable.
Deliver a professional Technical Data Package that includes a 3D model, exploded views, and clear manufacturing drawings using basic GD&T to show how parts fit and function together.

Basic 3D CAD Proficiency: You should be comfortable navigating a 3D CAD environment (Fusion 360, SolidWorks, or similar). Specifically, you need to know how to create 2D sketches, fully constrain them and perform base operations like extrudes, revolves, and fillets. Note: If you have not used CAD software before, we provide weekly 30-minute refresher videos and training materials to help you catch up, but you must be willing to invest extra effort to master these fundamentals alongside the project work.

Basic Mechanical Physics: You don’t need to be an expert in complex math, but you should have a basic intuition for how objects react to force and understand why parts fail. You should be able to understand the difference between stress and strain, basic material properties, and intuitively grasp how forces transfer through a load path. If you have completed a standard "Mechanics of Materials" course, you are well-prepared.

3D Visualization & "Blueprint" Basics: You need to be able to visualize how 2D sketches translate into 3D volumes and vice versa. You need the ability to read and generate basic 2D orthographic projections (Top, Front, Side views) to clearly communicate your design intent to a manufacturer.

An Engineering Problem-Solver Mindset: You need the willingness to prioritize function over form. You should be prepared to iterate your designs based on calculation and physical requirements rather than aesthetic preference alone and be ready to adopt a structured design methodology.

projects.title: From Zero to Prototype: Bring Your Software Startup Idea to Life

content.text: Develop a software startup idea into a prototype using Figma by researching the problem, understanding users, and designing effective solutions iteratively.

You have a software product idea that you want to develop into a real product. Where do you even start? The truth is that it’s straightforward once you learn the process. It helps if you have Computer Science, Software Engineering, Design or Business or have previously acquired skills in one of these areas. 

Every day, talented people work on countless software startup ideas, yet most fail. Using tools like the design process and user research can help teams move quickly and avoid common pitfalls that derail projects. In this Build project, you’ll take on the role of a digital product designer, applying the design process to software development. You’ll start by researching users, move through ideation sessions, and ultimately build a prototype to pitch to a wider audience. The outcome will be an MVP (Minimum Viable Product)—not necessarily a finished product, but a foundation to introduce the essential tools and methods needed to build one successfully. 

After 8 weeks, you’ll be able to apply this process to develop product ideas in any industry and tackle various problems. If you’re pursuing product manager or product designer roles, this project will also serve as a valuable addition to your portfolio. 

Considering the recent advances in AI, students will be encouraged to use the latest tools such as Cursor/Windsurf and Bolt/Vercel v0, if it suits their existing background and skills. LLMs usage is highly encouraged for everything we do in or outside class.  1b:T40a,Arun
Turn a software idea into a digital prototype using Figma.
Conduct user research to understand the needs, behaviors, and contexts of software users.
Generate creative concepts for software applications based on user insights and design thinking.
Pitch your software product to an audience using clear, compelling storytelling techniques.
Design Tool Experience: Familiarity with a design tool like Balsamiq or Figma, used in at least one project (academic or personal).
Presentation Skills: Experience using presentation tools such as PowerPoint or Keynote for at least two presentations.

Industry Knowledge: Some understanding of the industry related to your product idea. For example, if you’re designing software for physicians, you should have basic knowledge of the medical field; otherwise, the idea may be out of scope.
User Access and Knowledge: Access to and familiarity with potential users, enabling you to conduct effective user research.

projects.title: From Zero to Window: Engineering a Window Production Line

content.text: Reimagine a real-world window production line using core manufacturing engineering principles. Tackle challenges like customer demand, budget limits, workspace efficiency (5S), quality control, and ergonomics—then design your own optimized solution from the ground up.

In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Manufacturing Engineer, a role that’s foundational across countless entry-level jobs in the manufacturing and industrial engineering sectors, especially in industries like automotive, aerospace, and building products, where production line optimization is key. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll design and model a scalable window production line that responds to real-world constraints like customer demand, budget limits, and operational efficiency. You’ll analyze existing production layouts, simulate improvements using lean tools, and develop a theoretical AutoCAD layout for a new line that balances cost, quality, and throughput. You'll become familiar with industry-standard methodologies like A3 project management, TAKT time calculations, 5S workspace organization, and capacity modeling tools. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real lean manufacturing engineering team.
Explore core and advanced manufacturing engineering concepts tailored to the window and door industry and gain insights into how real products are designed, built, and optimized.
Simulate real-world manufacturing strategy projects using virtual tools and collaborative problem-solving, experience the thrill of engineering decision-making in action.

Build practical skills in capacity analysis, process mapping, and lean manufacturing tools like A3 project management and TAKT time—essential techniques used by top engineers to streamline production.
Use online modeling tools to compare current vs. future production states and visualize performance improvements.
Design your own theoretical production line in AutoCAD, bringing your ideas to life with professional-grade software.
Create and analyze forecast models in Excel, learning how engineers predict demand and plan resources
Intermediate AutoCAD Skills: Layer creation, block creation, annotative text, applying dimensions to scale, and modifying existing layouts independently

A3 Problem Solving Framework: Identifying the problem statement, laying out objectives, deciding what is in-scope and out-scope, determining countermeasure steps and lastly, setting realistic dates to complete milestones
Project Planning and Team Collaboration: Experience working in teams to build project timelines, delegate tasks, and present engineering decisions clearly and professionally

projects.title: Thinking in Data: Optimizing Decision-Making Through Databases, SQL, and AI

content.text: Design relational databases, write and optimize SQL queries, and integrate artificial intelligence to solve real-world data challenges.

In this 8-week project, you will explore the fundamentals of databases and SQL through practical, hands-on learning. You will design relational database schemas, write basic SQL queries to manipulate and retrieve data, and gain an introduction to AI concepts by preparing data for simple analysis. This Build Project is designed for beginners and focuses on building a strong foundation in database management and data analysis skills, preparing students for entry-level tasks in the field.

This Build Project goes far beyond simply learning how to manage databases and write SQL queries. Through a practical and strategic approach, you will discover how organizing and structuring information reflects a logical mindset that not only optimizes data management but also enhances decision-making and problem-solving in any field. You will learn to critically analyze information, design efficient solutions, and develop a structured way of thinking that will help you tackle complex challenges in technology, business, and everyday life. Because understanding databases is not just about managing information—it’s about learning to think logically and strategically in a data-driven world.
Design and implement relational database schemas using tools like entity-relationship diagrams (ERDs) to model real-world scenarios.
Write, optimize, and troubleshoot SQL queries, including advanced techniques like joins, subqueries, and indexing.
Develop and execute stored procedures and triggers for database automation and event-driven operations.
Prepare and clean datasets using SQL to meet the requirements of machine learning models.
Integrate SQL with AI libraries to perform predictive analysis and solve industry
Basic familiarity using spreadsheets or tabular data: Understanding how data is organized in rows and columns (e.g., Excel or Google Sheets).
Eagerness to learn new technical skills: No prior coding experience is required, but a willingness to learn SQL syntax and database concepts is essential.
Basic logical thinking and problem-solving: Ability to break down simple problems into smaller steps and follow structured instructions.
Basic understanding of data relationships: Familiarity with the concept of how items in one dataset might relate to items in another (e.g., customer orders linked to customer IDs).

projects.title: Editing Life’s Blueprint: Stem Cell Solutions for Human Disease

content.text: Explore stem cell biology and genome engineering through the lens of human disease, crafting your own concept map linking gene expression, cell signaling pathways, and differentiation outcomes in clinically relevant cell types.

The cause of most human diseases are born out of cellular malfunctions, which are directly linked to gene structure and function. This Build Project addresses the challenge of genetic manipulation of human stem cells to revolutionize regenerative medicine and cell-based therapies. You will learn how to integrate advanced genome engineering tools (CRISPR/Cas9, prime editing) with stem cell biology to, reprogram, differentiate, and genetically modify human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), enabling breakthroughs in disease modeling and therapeutic development.

By tackling key steps in this process, such as choosing the right gene-editing strategy for a given target, derivation of genetically modified iPSCs clones and the manipulation of cell signaling pathways to guide the production of specific cell types by in vitro iPSC differentiation, you will gain a solid understanding of the current biotechnological challenges for the creation of clinically relevant cells and tissues. By the end of the project, you will create a slide deck where you will design a concept map linking gene editing, gene expression, cell signaling pathways, and differentiation outcomes in clinically relevant cell types. This interdisciplinary training will empower you to design innovative genome engineering strategies, refine cell differentiation protocols, and develop the professional expertise needed to participate in cell therapy projects, addressing genetic disorders, cancer, and degenerative diseases.
Understand the biomedical capabilities of human stem cells and the fundamental concepts for the generation of adult human cell types through the process of human embryonic development.
Identify the key laboratory methods necessary for cell reprograming for the creation of induced pluripotent stem cells generation (iPSC).
Acquire the foundational knowledge required for working with iPSC for in vitro cell culture, as well as directed and guided cell differentiation.
Design CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing workflows for the accurate and deliberate manipulation of genetic information, as a critical tool for biomedical research, gene therapy and cell therapy.

Basic knowledge of molecular biology, mainly the relationship between DNA, RNA and proteins: You must know how DNA is transcribed to RNA and translated to proteins. You should understand the structure and function of nucleic acids, the processes of replication, transcription, and translation, and how genes code for proteins.

A general understanding of embryonic development and cell differentiation: You should comprehend how a fertilized egg develops through stages (cleavage, gastrulation) and how unspecialized cells (stem cells) differentiate into specialized cell types.

Comprehension of molecular biology techniques, such as PCR, electrophoresis and DNA sequencing: You should understand the methods of PCR DNA amplification, nucleic acid separation by size and determining the nucleotide sequence. You must know how these techniques are applied in research and diagnostics.

projects.title: Geotechnical Monitoring and Safety Assessment in Mining Operation

content.text: Get the knowledge and practical skills required for geotechnical monitoring and safety assessment in mining and civil operations using advanced technologies such as ground-based radar, InSAR, and QGIS.

Geotechnical monitoring is a critical aspect of mining operations, ensuring the safety and stability of mine structures by measuring and analyzing ground movements, stress, and other geotechnical parameters. This Build Project introduces students to fundamental geotechnical monitoring techniques and tools, empowering them to understand and manage potential geological hazards within a mine environment. Through hands-on experience and data analysis, you will gain a foundational understanding of how geotechnical monitoring plays a key role in enhancing mine safety.
By the end of the project, you will be able to:
- Understand geotechnical terms and concepts, like opportunities and risks.
- Identify and analyze simple patterns in geotechnical data, such as detecting early warning signs of potential ground movement.
- Apply data mapping and visualization skills through basic QGIS exercises, demonstrating how spatial data can be used in monitoring and hazard assessment.
- Prepare a structured technical report, presenting a data collection and analysis findings.
Knowledge of basic geotechnical engineering principles, including the engineering design process, risk assessment and safety, and rock mechanics.
Willingness to learn GIS tools to interpret results and draw conclusions.
Ability to understand ground movement trends from geotechnical monitoring instruments such as piezometers, ground-based radars, and GNSS.

projects.title: Giving Voice to Innovation: The Language of Tech Brands

content.text: Learn how to explain technology company innovations clearly and engagingly for the public, and practice real-world PR writing and media communication tasks.

As artificial intelligence, robotics, and quantum computing continue to advance, technology companies are increasingly in need of communication professionals who can clearly explain complex innovations to the public. This type of work is especially common in tech public relations and entry-level communication roles. In this Build Project, you will step into the role of a Public Relations Specialist to write tech news stories, learn how to craft product introductions and crisis response materials, and design clear, engaging messaging for typical communication scenarios faced by tech companies. With guidance from an experienced industry leader, you will analyze the communication strategies of leading tech brands and complete a polished, public-facing article—such as a founder profile, a science-based news feature, or a press release for a new product. You will also gain hands-on experience with industry-standard tools like Google Docs, Medium, and Canva while working in a simulated tech communications environment, laying a strong foundation for a future career in the field.b:
Identify common communication channels and methods used by technology companies to share information with the public.
Summarize key features or benefits of a new technology in clear, simple language.
Write a basic press release and company news update for a technology product or event.
Create a simple media communication plan for a product launch or company announcement.
Use tools like Google Docs and Canva to design and share digital communication materials.
Basic written communication skills in English: You should be able to write clear, complete sentences and organize your ideas in a logical order.
Familiarity with Google Docs: You will draft and revise your article using Google Docs throughout the project.
Interest in technology and how it is communicated: You should be curious about how companies explain new products or innovations to the public.
Ability to find and understand information: You should feel comfortable searching company websites or news articles to gather background details for your writing.
Openness to feedback: You will revise your work based on peer and instructor comments, so a willingness to reflect and improve is important.

projects.title: Build Renewable Energy Investment Models with Clarity and Confidence

content.text: Act as an investor evaluating a clean‑power project by analyzing revenues, costs, and financing assumptions in Excel, and communicating results through a concise investment memo.

Financing renewable energy projects is one of the most common entry points for analysts and associates in the clean energy industry, making project finance skills essential for early-career professionals. In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Renewable Energy Investor and build a project finance model while preparing an investment memo that reflects real industry practices. You'll learn to structure an underwriting model, model debt and tax equity financing, and forecast long-term revenues and costs. You’ll become familiar with Excel-based financial modeling, scenario testing, and compliance metrics like DSCR, all in an environment simulating the operations of a real renewable energy finance team.
Gain hands-on experience creating and interpreting simple financial models used by professionals in renewable energy and infrastructure private equity
Learn how money is raised, invested and repaid in solar and wind projects from lenders, investors, and developers.
Practice presenting project economics and investment risks clearly, the way fund managers, bankers, and asset managers do.

Starting with an initial company introduction, you will develop a deep understanding of the company's business model, analyze its market position and competitive landscape, conduct detailed financial analysis using Excel, and ultimately determine whether this represents an exciting investment opportunity. You will learn to think critically about tech business quality, build full-stack investing analyses, and synthesize these views into compelling investment memos and presentations. These skills directly connect to entry-level roles in venture capital, private equity, investment banking, and/or corporate development.
Analyze a startup's financial and operating metrics using standard financial statements and/or customer data to understand revenue streams, margin structure, and unit economics.
Perform comprehensive market research on emerging industries to assess competitive landscapes and market opportunities.
Create compelling investment memos that synthesize research findings and present a clear investment thesis.
Develop effective presentation skills to communicate investment recommendations to stakeholders.

Basic mathematics background (Intro-level classes in Calculus and/or Linear Algebra, Intro Statistics).
Some familiarity with Excel (you're comfortable with basic data entry, simple formulas like SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, INDEX).
Strong written & verbal communication skills.
Critical thinking & analytical reasoning abilities.
Intellectual curiosity and passion for technology businesses & investing.
Knowledge or awareness of basic valuation methods (multiples, DCF fundamentals).

fellows.name: Hanseul Nam
fellows.bio:

projects.title: How Crime Works: Exploring Law in Action

content.text: Examine criminal theory, legal principles, defense strategies, and societal impacts through case studies and discussions.

Ever wondered what it takes to build a criminal case from start to finish? In this Build project, you'll step into the role of a legal analyst to dissect and build a comprehensive case portfolio on a mock criminal case, mirroring the analytical work common in law firms and public defender offices. Under the guidance of an experienced industry professional, you'll analyze key elements of the case, assess possible defenses, map out trial procedures, and craft a verdict and sentencing recommendation based on criminal law principles. You’ll gain hands-on experience with fundamental legal techniques like case classification, evidence assessment, and procedural mapping, all within a simulated judicial process.  

By the end of the project, you’ll develop a case analysis portfolio covering each stage of a criminal case, from classification to sentencing recommendations. You’ll present your findings in a legal brief format, simulating the concise and persuasive style of professional legal writing. 
 
This project offers a valuable, real-world experience for anyone interested in understanding the building blocks of criminal justice and applying legal concepts in practice.

projects.title: Insights to Interface: Designing User Centered Digital Experiences

content.text: Optimize the user experience of an existing digital product, through a complete UX design process, from user research and usability evaluation to high-fidelity UI design and interactive prototyping.

We interact with countless digital products every day - from mobile apps and websites to digital platforms that support how we work, shop, communicate, and navigate daily life. While some experiences feel intuitive and seamless, others create friction through confusing interactions, inefficient workflows, or usability challenges that impact thousands, sometimes millions of users at scale.

In this 8-week project, you will step into the role of a UX consultant and tackle those problems head-on. You will select an existing digital product you use regularly and work through a complete, professional UX redesign process - from research and analysis all the way to high-fidelity design and prototyping.

Starting with a structured heuristic evaluation and usability audit, you will identify key friction points and usability concerns within the current experience before moving into user research and empathy mapping to better understand the people behind the interactions. Using those insights, you will define design opportunities and translate them into improved experiences through user flows, high-fidelity UI designs, and interactive prototypes.

Throughout the project, you will learn how to work within an existing product ecosystem while balancing usability, accessibility, visual consistency, and interaction design principles. The experience is designed to mirror the end-to-end workflow of modern UX and product design teams, helping you build practical, portfolio-ready skills that directly align with entry-level roles in UX Design, Product Design, and Digital Product Development - some of the fastest-growing careers in today’s technology-driven workforce.
Perform foundational user research activities including user interviews, empathy mapping, and synthesis of qualitative insights to identify real usability problems in an existing digital product.

Build an interactive clickable prototype in Figma that communicates a complete user journey for a key task.

projects.title: Introduction to Drug Discovery

content.text: Learn about different pieces of the puzzle of the drug discovery process by developing drug candidates that target thymidylate kinase from Plasmodium falciparum (PfTMK) to tackle Malaria.

The goal of this Build Project is to do a deep dive on what is involved in a drug discovery project through focusing on developing drug candidates targeting thymidylate kinase from Plasmodium falciparum (PfTMK) to tackle malaria. You will navigate different stages of the drug discovery process, what techniques can be used at different stages, what to expect at different stages, what potential challenges are, and how to tackle challenges that arise. In this Build Project, you will learn the principles behind a wide spectrum of state-of-the-art technologies utilized in the drug discovery process and understand which tools can be used to address specific questions. Knowledge from this project will greatly benefit those who are interested in a career in drug development. By the end of this Build Project, you will have constructed a comprehensive slide deck illustrating your thought and decision-making process on how you would tackle this challenging drug discovery project.
Understand the general workflow of the drug discovery process: protein expression and purification, hit identification, hit characterization, and hit-to-lead process.
Gain a clear understanding about the principles behind powerful biophysical techniques (such as SPR, DLS, and DSF and when to use them) and data-driven decision-making.
Learn the principles behind powerful biochemical techniques in the drug discovery process (such as NADH-coupled assay, and ADP-Glo assay and when to use them) and data evaluation.
Learn the principles behind structural biology and its involvement within the structure-activity relationship in drug discovery projects.
Understand principles behind cell-based assays (such as NanoBRET assay) and animal studies, and how they contribute to the drug discovery process.
Learn about later stages of a drug discovery project, such as animal studies – when they should be carried out and what considerations to take.
Knowledge of molecular biology – more specifically, proteins: what they are, what they do.
Understanding of biochemistry, biophysics, structural biology, and cell biology on a conceptual level.
Critical thinking and decision-making – what is the most rational technique to use facing specific problems.

projects.title: Introduction to Industrial Automation Systems and PLC’s

content.text: Design and simulate a basic industrial automation system using Programmable Logic Controller “ PLC” to understand how smart factories streamline real-world operations.

In this hands-on Build Project, you will dive into the exciting world of industrial automation by designing and developing a real-world automation and control system. Through research-based learning, you will explore cutting-edge tools like Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), sensors, and actuators, while using simulation software to test and validate their designs. Guided by industry-relevant scenarios, students will solve complex challenges, such as optimizing manufacturing processes or ensuring system safety. By the end of the project, they will gain practical experience in system design, troubleshooting, and technical communication skills highly sought after in entry-level roles such as automation engineers, control system designers, and manufacturing specialists in today’s rapidly evolving U.S. workforce.
Utilize Simulation Tools: Apply software such as MATLAB, Simulink, or TIA Portal to simulate, test, and validate automation system designs.
Integrate Sensors and Actuators: Demonstrate the ability to select, integrate, and troubleshoot sensors, actuators, and other control system components for industrial applications.
Apply Problem-Solving Techniques: Diagnose and resolve challenges in control system design, utilizing systematic troubleshooting and optimization methods.
Communicate Technical Solutions: Prepare and present professional documentation, schematics, and project findings to effectively convey technical designs and their real-world applications.
Design Functional Control Systems: Create and document automation solutions using Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) with Ladder Logic or other industry-relevant programming languages.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Strong problem-solving.
A professional, hands-on style with the ability to work independently and as a team player, to take initiative, and manage multiple tasks and projects at a time.
Basic Understanding of Electrical Engineering Principles: Familiarity with circuit design, basis- level coding, control systems, and electrical components.
Willingness to Learn: A proactive mindset to explore new tools, techniques, and concepts relevant to the project.

projects.title: Investment Analyses for Portfolio Restructuring and Rebalance

content.text: Evaluating the current makeup of the investment portfolio and using the profitability/valuation ratios, and risk metrics, to design a strategy to align the portfolio to the current business and economic cycle.

With the US economy and population now being dominated by baby boomers (the demographic cohort born during the mid-40s and mid-60s), we face a significantly high number of individuals retiring from the workforce. In addition, we are in the middle of the biggest wealth transfer in the history of the U.S. This presents a great opportunity for individuals with skills to offer financial and investment advice.  

In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Financial and Investment Research Analyst. You will showcase the ability to evaluate the current makeup of the investment portfolio using the profitability/valuation ratios and risk metrics to develop and design an investment strategy to align the portfolio to the current business and economic cycle. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll compute the various investment ratios and statistical measurements used in portfolio construction and analysis. Also, you will evaluate the stock's common types of performance measurements and intrinsic value and explain how portfolio risk is used to develop efficient frontier/portfolios. You'll become familiar with industry tools/techniques/methodologies like Modern Portfolio Theory, Capital Asset Pricing Model, Ratio Analysis, and Efficient Market Hypothesis Concepts. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real Financial and Investment Research Analyst.
Analyze the risk and reward characteristics of each investment and investment type by applying statistical tools/formulas.
Identify and evaluate how investment vehicles are taxed and how taxes will impact the investment decision-making process when seen in conjunction with a client's situation.
Produce a side-by-side comparison of the various investment options to identify undervalued, fairly valued, and overvalued investments.
Develop portfolio strategies and recommendations for portfolio rebalance.
Familiarity and existing exposure to basic statistical concepts (mean, median, mode, standard deviation, etc.) and data visualization techniques (bar graphs, scatterplots, pie and donut charts, etc.)
An inclination to learn about the various investment evaluation techniques used in comparing two or more investments.
Basic knowledge and experience of using Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
A good command of verbal and written communication.

projects.title: Create a Venture Capital Investment Memo for a Gaming Startup

content.text: Pressure-test performance assumptions with Excel, synthesize industry research, and translate insights into an interview-ready report, defending your conclusions in a mock investment committee setting.

Any young career specialists who want to work in Venture Capital find it hard to understand how to break into this industry. One of the things that help a lot is having a prior VC experience. In this Build Project, you will wear the hat of a Venture Capital Analyst and prepare an investment memo for a potential gaming startup to perform financial, operational, and market due diligence. Under the supervision of an experienced Build Fellow, you will learn how a potential gaming startup investment opportunity will be analyzed and discussed to ultimately decide whether or not to invest. You will become familiar with financial modeling, operational modeling and various research methodologies that will aid you in your conclusion. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real investment committee in a venture capital firm.
Learn how to create work products that are formatted well and presentable in a workplace environment.
Learn how a potential gaming startup investment opportunity will be analyzed and discussed to ultimately decide whether or not to invest.
Become familiar with financial modeling, operational modeling and various research methodologies that will aid you in your conclusion.

Basic knowledge of Word: you should be able to edit a document to make it readable and visually appealing for others.

projects.title: LangChain for Beginners: An Introduction to LLM Application Development

content.text: This workshop introduces beginners to building simple applications with large language models using LangChain.

This project offers a hand-on introduction to building applications with large language models (LLMs) using LangChain. You will learn how to set up your development environment, interact with LLMs through simple prompts, and understand the foundational concepts behind LLM-powered assistants and chatbots. As you progress, you’ll experiment with creating and refining prompts, connecting user questions to language model responses, and exploring how basic workflows can be built using LangChain’s chains.

The emphasis throughout is on building foundational understanding, enabling you to see how LLMs and LangChain integrate to create practical, real-world applications. By the end of the project, you will have gained practical experience in working with language models and LangChain, and you’ll be able to demonstrate your learning by building a simple, interactive application that showcases your new skills.
Understand how to use LangChain to interact with language models.
Build simple LLM applications such as personal assistants and chatbots.
Apply LLMs to your proprietary data for specialized tasks.
Knowledge of Python programming.
Familiarity with large language models (LLMs).
Interest in AI Solutions.
