projects.title: Inside the Legal Mind: Build Your First Case Analysis and Legal Memo

content.text: Learn how lawyers think by breaking down judicial opinions, interpreting the law, and using your analysis to craft a clear, well‑structured memo that demonstrates your ability to advocate effectively.

This project is designed for students who aspire to work in the legal industry. Practicing law has its unique features that students cannot know until they get a hands-on experience of what it’s like. How is “legal writing” different from writing any other essays or research papers? How is reading case law and court decisions different from any other papers? What does "legal analysis" look like? Law Students spend an entire year (or more) to learn these skills. The project allows you to get a head start in gaining these skills, in a more simplified, beginner-friendly way. You will develop a legal memo as a final deliverable, which will include your analysis of cases, and its application to the matter at hand, and your position in advocating for your client. It can be used as a writing sample which will be handy in applying for law schools and/or internships or other law office positions that do not require an attorney license. At the end of the 8-weeks session, you will feel more confident applying for law schools or jobs in the legal industry.b:["$"
By the end of the project, you will be able to:   Understand what it is like to be a law student and the daily work of an attorney working in different areas of the legal industry.
Analyze case law and interpret the Court’s decisions and underlying reasonings.
Prepare a legal brief/memo by applying your legal analysis to the factual matters at hand.
Advocate for your client based on your legal research and analysis.
For you to be successful in this project, you will need:  Interest in the legal industry and the willingness to learn about the skills and techniques needed to work in the industry.
Past experience in reading and interpreting complex written work, and the ability to point out the relevant issues.
Some exposure to conducting research, including how to utilize key words.
Oral and written communication skills, being able to articulate your thoughts.
Desire to communicate with others, to share your thoughts, discuss, and debate.

projects.title: Law School Writing and Advocacy

content.text: Gain the essential advocacy, analytical and legal writing skills needed for law school success through this preparatory program designed to guide you from admissions to your first year of law school.

This is a pre-law project designed for college freshmen and sophomores to develop a practical understanding of lawyering and build analytical and advocacy skills. The first weeks of the project will focus on demystifying the law school admissions process. You will then develop an appellate brief that can be used as a writing sample for your future career endeavors. 

You will also present oral arguments in a simulated courtroom environment. This project emphasizes research, writing, and oral advocacy, providing you with the opportunity to analyze complex legal cases, formulate well-reasoned arguments, and participate in structured debates. More importantly, this project will serve as a preview of what you can expect during your year of law school. 

You will refine your analytical thinking, writing, and public speaking abilities. By the end of this project, you will have gained critical skills in research, writing, and argumentation, directly applicable to entry-level roles in law, public policy, and various sectors that value clear communication and analytical precision.
Conduct legal research, read cases, and properly apply legal frameworks and precedents.
Write clearly and persuasively, as is expected from an attorney.
Advocate on behalf of clients, both in writing and orally in the courtroom.
An interest in a legal career: This project is designed for students with a basic understanding of the rule of law and the roles that lawyers, judges and policy makers occupy.

Logical reasoning: As a lawyer, you will need to draw on the skills of analyzing, evaluating, constructing, and refuting arguments based on logic, regardless of how you may subjectively feel about an issue.
Reading comprehension: the practice of law revolves around extensive reading of highly varied, dense, argumentative, and expository texts (for example, cases, statutes, deposition transcripts).

Intellectual curiosity: Students will be asked to explore various areas of legal practice, conduct research on cutting edge legal issues, and craft arguments from various, sometimes opposing perspectives.

Public speaking: at the end of the project, students will be expected to present oral arguments in front of the entire class in the context of a mock trial, where students will argue their case in front of a judge.
Attention to detail is essential to a lawyer’s credibility.

projects.title: Lawyer for a Day: Build a Legal Case and Argue It in a Mock Trial

content.text: You will step into the role of a lawyer as you analyze a fictional dispute, draft a persuasive legal brief, and argue your case in a live mock trial simulation.

Think of this Project as a day in the life (likely a month) of a lawyer. You will learn the basics of how the US Legal system operates, how laws are interpreted, how to analyze decisions of different US courts and how to apply this law to factual circumstances. You will acquire skills vital for a career in the legal profession such as analysis, research, legal writing and oral advocacy. You will then apply these skills to a fictional legal dispute and draft a legal brief. These skills are helpful for those of you contemplating taking the LSATs. These skills would also benefit those of you considering careers in fields such as communications, business management and consultancy.
Analyse a dispute and determine whether a legal claim can be made
Understand the nuances of the US legal system
Marshal facts and present them in the most persuasive manner
Analyse a legal decision and present legal arguments in a trial simulation

Critical thinking & analytical reasoning: to identify key issues in the fact pattern, evaluate both sides, and build logical arguments from evidence and rules.
Basic legal reading/research literacy: comfort reading simplified statutes/cases and pulling out the rule/holding to apply to the fictional dispute.

projects.title: Design, Deploy, and Secure Cloud Infrastructure on AWS

content.text: Experiment with the fundamental principles associated with software development in the Amazon Web Services cloud using Infrastructure as Code (Iac) and Terraform.

Cloud operations and DevOps have become heavily critical to hosting and running any high-performance web applications that can scale as the user demand increases. This Build Project will introduce you to basic cloud principles, explain some of the best practices and walk you through a couple of hands-on exercises to prepare you to dive deeper into the world of cloud engineering.

By the end of the 8-weeks project, you will develop a sound foundation of cloud principles. You will develop architecture diagrams and implement those on the AWS cloud platform for hosting a basic web application. Finally, you will be tasked to develop and present a migration strategy for a company that wants to move their web architecture from On-Prem to the AWS Cloud.

Since most software organizations use some form of the cloud or another, having these foundational principles can help you understand the company's software infrastructure as well as stand out from your competition.
Identify different approaches to hosting web applications including on-premise, Hybrid and cloud.
Deploy cloud infrastructure resources and maintain them using the principles of Infrastructure as Code and Terraform.
Explore hosting containerized applications (AWS ECS and EKS) and using serverless technologies (AWS Lambda).
Develop a multi-zone available, highly reliable and resilient cloud architecture to host a simple web application.
Access to the internet.
An AWS Free-Tier Account
Ability to run basic commands in Terminal/Bash/Shell - Familiarity with running CLI commands (Any basic IT course would be enough)
Understanding of what a Web Application is and its various components

projects.title: Learn Graph Neural Network Through Real Examples

Graphs are powerful data structures that can model complex relationships in various domains such as social networks, molecular structures, and citation networks. We'll cover foundational concepts and progress to advanced topics such as Graph Attention Networks (GATs), Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), and GraphSAGE. You will apply your knowledge through three mini-projects: a course scheduler, model interactions in communities, molecular structure & citation networks. projects.title: Legal Analysis and Writing: Legal Memorandums and Briefs

You will learn legal writing to organize research, create outlines, and draft legal documents such as memorandums and briefs at the end of the project. projects.title: Law in Events Planning: Build the Legal Strategy for a Major Cybersecurity Conference

content.text: Get introduced to the role of lawyers advising event organizers by examining key legal issues involved in planning and managing live, virtual, and hybrid events while applying legal principles through practical simulations.

This 8-week Build Project provides a comprehensive introduction to the legal principles that govern the planning and management of modern events. Students will explore the legal framework surrounding event operations and examine how legal professionals help organizations navigate regulatory requirements, manage risk, protect stakeholders, and ensure compliance throughout the event lifecycle.

Throughout the project, you will step into the role of legal counsel by developing a comprehensive legal strategy for a large-scale cybersecurity conference involving industry experts, sponsors, vendors, and government representatives. The simulated event includes keynote presentations, breakout sessions, live demonstrations, and networking receptions, providing realistic scenarios through which to apply legal concepts in a practical context.

As the project progresses, you will connect legal theory with professional practice by examining topics such as contracts, permits and licensing, liability and risk management, insurance, intellectual property, and crisis management. You will also explore emerging legal issues affecting today's events, including cybersecurity incident liability, vendor data management, public safety obligations, and content and branding rights.

By completing weekly exercises and assignments, you will develop a comprehensive legal event plan that demonstrates how legal analysis, risk assessment, regulatory compliance, and strategic decision-making contribute to the successful planning and execution of complex live, virtual, and hybrid events.
Apply legal theory to real-world event scenarios
Draft and analyze key legal documents
Understand regulatory and compliance requirements
Assess and mitigate legal risks
Think critically about the intersection of law, business, entertainment, and public policy.
Contract Law: Basic structure of a contract (offer, acceptance, consideration, terms)

Legal System Awareness: a general sense of local/state regulations and the role of law in public safety and regulation

projects.title: Let’s build a business idea, plan and financial pitch

Brainstorming a business idea and then crafting a business plan for a new start up idea is a critical first step often looked over by first time founders. In this Build Project, we’ll be working on exactly this. We’ll do a business plan that lays the foundation for the founder’s vision as well as develops a greater understanding of all key matrix required to launch a business successfully. Added to that, we’ll develop a set of financial documents that clearly illustrate the capital requirements and predicated returns. Then, we’ll work on a polished Pitch deck and elevator pitch to round out all you will need to raise your first round of capital.

The skills developed in this project will be clear and concise communication tools and networking blueprint as well as financial modelling techniques and general financial principles. The ability to construct an effective elevator pitch and complete Pitch Deck will also be developed. This will all be housed in a complete business plan developed that clearly describes the business and its growth and scalability.

projects.title: Leverage Artificial Intelligence to Make Investments in Equity Securities

content.text: Analyze a publicly traded company and develop a full investment thesis by combining financial models, qualitative research, and a professional pitch.

In this hands-on project, you will step into the role of an equity research analyst and learn how professional investors evaluate companies. You will select a publicly traded stock, analyze its financial statements, assess its competitive positioning, and build a simple valuation model to determine whether it is undervalued or overvalued. Alongside traditional methods of financial analysis, you will also learn how to use AI tools to streamline research — from summarizing company filings and industry reports to running sentiment checks on news and earnings calls. By the end of the project, you will have produced a polished equity research report and delivered an investor-style presentation that combines financial modeling, qualitative insights, and AI-supported research.

Interest in financial markets and business strategy — curiosity about how companies operate and how investors decide where to allocate capital.

These skills will help you understand how to analyze, evaluate, and develop practical strategies to optimize cost, mitigate risk, and improve efficiency in the international supply chain of a U.S. company.

projects.title: Mapping the Bay Area AI Data Ecosystem

content.text: Analyze the Bay Area AI ecosystem through public information and simple data analysis, then build and present a focused investigation on a question you choose.

Modern AI systems depend not only on models and compute, but also on data: how it is collected, structured, filtered, labeled, synthesized, and evaluated. In this Build Project, you will work as a data scientist and technology analyst to understand the Bay Area AI ecosystem, learn how frontier labs, startups, research communities, and data providers fit together, and then choose a narrow question of your own to investigate. You will turn public information into a small, structured dataset or evidence table, use a simple spreadsheet or Python-based analysis to identify patterns, and develop a clear point of view supported by data. Possible directions include mapping data-for-AI startups, comparing public datasets or benchmarks, analyzing recurring data skills in AI job postings, or studying how a selected AI domain obtains and evaluates data; the emphasis is on industry exposure, good data-science habits, and clear analytical communication rather than building a large or technically complex model.
Explain the major parts of the Bay Area AI ecosystem and where data science and data-for-AI work fit within it.
Distinguish common types of data used in modern AI, including training data, post-training data, evaluation data, human feedback, synthetic data, and multimodal data.
Turn public information into a small, structured dataset by defining variables, recording sources, and cleaning the data consistently.
Use descriptive statistics and simple visualizations to answer a focused question and identify meaningful patterns.
Communicate an evidence-backed conclusion, including limitations, through a concise professional presentation.
Basic quantitative reasoning: you should be comfortable working with percentages, averages, comparisons, and simple charts.
Experience with tabular data: you should be able to open a spreadsheet, understand rows and columns, and sort or filter a table; prior Python experience is helpful but not required.
Web research and source tracking: you should be able to find public information, summarize it in your own words, and record where each data point came from.
Clear written and verbal communication: you should be willing to explain what a chart shows, what it does not show, and what conclusion you draw from it.

projects.title: Application of Markowitz Portfolio Theory to build your own portfolio

content.text: The primary objective of this project is to implement and apply the Markowitz Portfolio Theory to construct diversified portfolios that strike an optimal balance between risk and return.

In the ever-evolving landscape of financial markets, constructing and managing portfolios that optimize returns while minimizing risk is a fundamental challenge for investors. The Markowitz Portfolio Theory, introduced by Nobel laureate Harry Markowitz, offers a pioneering framework for portfolio optimization. This project aims to leverage Markowitz's model to build and back-test portfolios, providing valuable insights into the construction of efficient investment strategies.

The primary objective of this project is to implement and apply the Markowitz Portfolio Theory to construct diversified portfolios that strike an optimal balance between risk and return. By utilizing historical financial data, we will back-test these portfolios to evaluate their performance under different market conditions.

projects.title: Mastering Financial Analysis: Excel-Based Valuation and Reporting

content.text: Analyze the financial health of a company through financial statement analysis and develop a viable valuation model using Discounted Cash Flow (DCF).

Financial analysis and valuation are essential skills used across industries to assess company performance, guide investment decisions, and support strategic planning. Through this hands-on Build Project, you will gain exposure to working with Excel, processing financial data, and performing advanced calculations such as DCF model and ratios. You’ll experience the daily tasks of a financial analyst, learning key techniques and methodologies that are essential for any professional in the field of finance and valuation.

In this project, you'll wear the hat of a Financial Analyst and analyze Balance Sheets, Income Statements, and Cash Flow Statements to assess the company’s financial health. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll calculate key financial ratios in Excel, and create financial projections. Using these projections, they’ll build a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model to estimate a company’s intrinsic value and test how valuation changes under different assumptions using basic sensitivity analysis. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real finance team.

Calculate and explain key financial ratios - including profitability, liquidity, solvency, and cash flow ratios - using Excel

Perform basic sensitivity analysis in Excel to test how changes in key assumptions affect valuation
Communicate financial insights clearly using charts, summary slides, and a final presentation

projects.title: Measuring & Predicting the Economy for Financial Markets

content.text: Learn how economists and market strategists use macroeconomic data and policy decisions to forecast short-term movements in stocks and bonds.

Financial markets respond quickly to new economic information such as inflation reports, jobs data, and policy announcements. Professional economists and market strategists often rely on simple empirical tools to interpret this information and form short-term expectations.

In this Build Project, you will learn how to use basic economic reasoning and simple regression techniques to analyze macroeconomic data and think about its implications for financial markets. The course emphasizes intuition and clarity rather than advanced mathematics. All quantitative work is done in Excel using straightforward, easy-to-follow methods.

Each session combines a short conceptual overview with hands-on exercises using real U.S. economic data. By the end of the project, you will produce a short-term macroeconomic forecast and explain what it could mean for stocks and bonds.

Have an interest in economics, finance, or financial markets.
Be familiar with basic concepts such as inflation, growth, and interest rates.
Feel comfortable working with Excel, including charts and formulas.

projects.title: Mechanical Engineering in the Pharmaceutical Industry: Filling Station for Liquid Drug Substances

content.text: Utilize Mechanical Engineering principles to conceptualize, design and conduct failure analysis on a filling station for liquid drug substances.

In the biopharmaceutical industry, ensuring precise and sterile filling processes is crucial, making it a central task for many entry-level roles. In this Build Project, you'll take on the role of a Mechanical Engineer, where you'll conceptualize, design, and conduct failure analysis for a cutting-edge mechanical filling station. Under the guidance of a seasoned industry expert, you'll tackle real-world challenges related to fluid dynamics, precision engineering, and regulatory compliance. You'll gain hands-on experience with industry-standard tools and methodologies such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), all within a simulated biopharma team environment that mirrors industry operations.
Understand how mechanical engineering and design intersects with regulatory and quality control standards specific to the pharmaceutical industry.
Leverage principles of mechanical engineering to perform failure analysis and risk assessments.
Explore sterile systems and aseptic design.

Familiarity with CAD or mechanical engineering design. You may use any tool to prepare your design, but you should have some familiarity with mechanical design concepts.

projects.title: Microbes in Action: Driving Soil Health for Regenerative Agriculture

content.text: Prepare a proposal/report on how to use microbial solutions to enhance soil health, boost crop productivity, and promote regenerative farming practices.

Healthy soils are alive, teeming with billions of microbes that quietly power our food systems. These microscopic allies include bacteria, fungi, and other microscopic organisms. They are essential for nutrient cycling, plant health, and long-term soil regeneration.

In this Build Project, you will learn how to identify soil microbes and understand their diversity using both visual and data-driven methods. You will explore their crucial role in releasing nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, improving soil structure, and protecting plants from pests and diseases. Through real-world examples from regenerative farming practices in diverse cropping systems such as oranges, almonds, and vegetable farming, you will learn how microbial bio-stimulants and biocontrol agents are transforming agriculture while reducing chemical inputs. By the end of the project, you will have the skills to assess soil microbial health, apply targeted microbial solutions, and design farm management strategies that enhance productivity, resilience, and environmental sustainability. You will summarize your learnings in a single integrated proposal that combines case study insights with a farm management plan for sustainable microbial solutions. You will either create a poster or PowerPoint presentation to share your work with the team members.
Understand soil microbial diversity and roles in supporting regenerative farming systems.
Select and apply microbial bio-stimulants to enhance soil fertility, crop growth, and resilience.
Utilize beneficial microbes for pest and disease management to reduce reliance on chemical inputs.
Assess and monitor soil microbial diversity using practical and data-driven approaches.
Integrate microbial data and solutions into farm management plans for sustainable, regenerative agriculture.

Soil: Basic knowledge regarding soil science (e.g., soil structure, organic matter, soil gradient)

projects.title: Mind Matters: Neurophysiological Basis of Mental Health

content.text: Acquire the scientific knowledge to develop key skills, strengthening your clinical practice and nurturing your personal mental well-being.

In this project, we'll go beyond the textbook to give you a critical, competitive edge: an in-depth understanding of the neuroscience of mental health and burnout. Over the course of 8 sessions, you will analyze the neurophysiological basis of mental health conditions, exploring brain function, neurotransmitter systems, and stress physiology to create a personalized, sustainable wellness plan. We will also delve into the neural circuits, chemical messengers, and stress responses that shape our well-being. By the end of the project, you will not only be better equipped to care for yourself and your peers but will also gain a unique perspective that is highly sought after in the modern medicine.
Understand the foundational neurobiological and psychosocial factors impacting physician mental health and apply evidence-based strategies for self-care and seeking support.
Enhance your knowledge of brain function, neurotransmitter systems, and stress physiology to better understand the etiology and maintenance of mental health conditions.
Understand the neurobiological underpinnings of mental health prevention and possess insights into the specific stressors impacting healthcare workers.
Gain practical strategies and insights to navigate the stressors of the medical learning environment and to recognize and respond effectively to mental health concerns in themselves and their peers.

Foster the development of personal resilience through an understanding of neurobiological and psychological mechanisms, ultimately enabling students to create sustainable wellness plans for their personal and professional lives.
General interest in developing a career in health care: This project is not limited to any specific branch since it focuses on the human aspect, rather than a purely technical one.

Basic knowledge in neurosciences and general psychology: You must have a basic knowledge of human anatomy and physiology, particularly related to the nervous system. This includes an understanding of: The basic structure of the brain (e.g., major lobes, limbic system), the function of neurons and synaptic transmission, core psychological concepts such as cognition, emotion, and behavior.

Critical reflection and self-awareness: Recognizing one's emotional responses is the first requirement to understanding them, this requires you to find your own limits and a willingness to engage in self-care-practices.
Effective communication: Demonstrated by practicing active listening, discussing conflicts, and the ability to deliver information in a sensitive manner.

projects.title: Molecular Insights and Environmental Factors in Fertility: Advancements in Reproductive Medicine

content.text: This project examines the molecular and environmental factors affecting fertility, focusing on advancements in clinical embryology and assisted reproductive technologies (ART) to improve reproductive success.

This project provides an immersive experience in the field of clinical embryology and fertility research. Students will delve into the science of human reproduction and in vitro fertilization (IVF) and its techniques, exploring how lifestyle modifications can improve treatment outcomes. Through research and analysis, participants will address real-world challenges in fertility treatments, such as patient education and evidence-based interventions.

Recent data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and other public health sources indicate that approximately 10–15% of couples experience infertility, with both male and female factors contributing significantly to reproductive challenges. Male infertility factors account for approximately 30–35% of infertility cases. These statistics underscore the growing need for advancements in fertility research, accessible treatment options, and increased public awareness of reproductive health.

The growing demand for fertility services has led to a booming fertility clinic industry, with the U.S. market projected to reach $14 billion by 2030 (Grand View Research). This surge reflects not only increased awareness and technological advancements but also a shift in societal trends, such as delayed parenthood and rising infertility rates.

By the end of the project, students will have developed foundational knowledge in clinical embryology, IVF laboratory principles, and fertility-related research methodologies applicable to careers in reproductive medicine and public health.

Gain proficiency in research methodologies specific to reproductive sciences
Develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills to address challenges in fertility treatments
Create data-driven recommendations to improve outcomes in reproductive medicine
Analyze molecular, environmental, and clinical factors influencing fertility and IVF outcomes.

Research and Analytical Skills
Critical Thinking

Technical Proficiency

projects.title: NetSim: Building a Simulated Computer System

content.text: Build a simplified computer system with WebSocket-connected components and a live React Flow dashboard to learn real-time messaging, Finite State Machines, and system integration.

In this Build Project, you’ll wear the hat of a Systems Engineer and build a networked computer simulation where each student develops a lightweight WebSocket client representing a system component (CPU, Memory, or I/O). Under the supervision of an experienced computer engineer, you’ll coordinate real-time communication between components, manage state transitions using finite state machines, and visualize live system activity through React Flow. You’ll gain hands-on experience with real-time protocols, FSM logic, and collaborative development workflows, all within an environment that mirrors the operations of a real software systems engineering team.

Send and receive structured real-time messages via WebSockets.
Simulate interactions between CPU, Memory, and I/O components.
Visualize live system interactions using React Flow.
Collaborate on a distributed system architecture with GitHub.

Familiarity with NodeJS and TypeScript.

projects.title: Private Investments: Build a Real-World Fund Analysis

projects.title: Process to Profit: Design an AI-Powered Improvement

content.text: Learn how to spot an inefficient business process, design a practical AI-powered improvement, and prove the impact with clear metrics and a simple Return on Investment (ROI) model.

Every organization has “hidden” inefficiencies—manual handoffs, slow approvals, repetitive work, and inconsistent decisions. These problems waste time and money, frustrate employees, and create worse experiences for customers. In this Build Project, you’ll act like a junior consultant helping a company improve one critical workflow (examples: customer support, hiring, invoice approvals, procurement, onboarding, reporting). You’ll pick a real-world company or organization to focus on, map how the process works today (“as-is”), and identify the biggest bottlenecks. Then you’ll design a practical AI-enabled improvement (for example: automating a repetitive task, helping staff make faster decisions, or improving quality/consistency). Finally, you’ll estimate the business impact using a simple ROI model, define the KPIs that would prove success, and create a dashboard mockup that shows how leaders would track results. projects.title: Propose a Design of an Automated System to Control a Bioreactor

content.text: Create a ladder logic program that automatically controls the operations of a bioreactor.

In biotech industry, bioreactors are essential for producing various products like pharmaceuticals, enzymes, biochemicals, and more through biological processes such as fermentation. An automated control system optimizes and regulates critical parameters (temperature, pH, agitation, aeration, etc.), that are necessary for the growth and productivity of microorganisms within the bioreactor. In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of Process Development Engineer and design an automated control system for a bioreactor. Under the supervision of an experienced Build Fellow, you'll learn how to create a ladder logic program to monitor and control various parameters for optimal growth conditions inside a bioreactor. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real DSP team.
How to design a ladder logic program to control the operations of an automated bioreactor system for Lygos’ pilot plant.
How to create a control system using ladder logic that monitors and regulates various parameters for optimal growth conditions inside a bioreactor.
How to successfully set up simulations to demonstrate the system’s functionality and its ability to maintain optimal conditions for bioreactor operation.
How to complete a comprehensive report document with the ladder logic program, including annotations and explanations of control strategies.
Commitment to start and finish the project, actively participate in all meetings, and work independently for ~1 hour/week.
Fundamental grasp of chemistry: you should understand the concept of temperature, pressure, pH, volume, etc.
Familiarity with programming elements such as inputs, outputs, numeral systems (decimal and binary), data types (Boolean, Integer, Floating point)

Other prerequisites: before the project starts, you'll need to have RSLogix Micro Starter Lite, RSlinx Classic Lite, and RSEmulate 500 installed on your computer. All these programs are free but can only be used on a Window computer.

projects.title: Develop a B2B Aggregator Platform Prototype for the Warehouse & Logistic Industry

content.text: Design an advanced, pioneering Business-to-Business (B2B) E-Commerce Aggregator platform to unify the Warehouse & Logistics industry.

This Build Project involves developing a B2B Aggregator platform for the Warehouse & Logistics industry. The platform will seamlessly integrate suppliers of services and products for the daily operational needs of Warehouse & Logistics industry, manage inventory, order fulfillment, and multi-channel e-commerce capabilities, addressing the complex challenges faced by modern businesses in the digital marketplace.

The current industry faces challenges such as disjointed operations, high pricing, and a lack of visibility on competitive suppliers, leading to a crisis in the supply chain, as witnessed during the recent pandemic. The objective of this project is to create a prototype that addresses these issues and provides end-to-end sourcing tracking capabilities for warehouse/logistics operations.

The platform features a user-friendly interface that caters to B2B operations, supporting complex pricing structures, bulk order management, and sophisticated supplier collaboration tools. The platform's architecture is built on scalable, cloud-native technologies, utilizing AWS services such as Lambda, DynamoDB, and API Gateway to ensure high performance, security, and reliability.
Understand E-commerce Platform Components for Warehouse/Logistics.
Design E-commerce Platform Prototype.
Create a Product Backlog for the platform, focusing on key features and high-priority user stories also termed as tasks/deliverables.
Prepare a detailed project plan and cover the various phases of SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle).
Design and architect a cloud-based solution for the platform.
Understand AWS services like AWS S3, AWS API Gateways and AWS DynamoDB.
Hands on training on Creating a Lambda, API Gateway, and integration with DynamoDB
Business Research and analysis skills that apply to Retailing, E-Commerce, Warehouse, logistics and Supply Chain industry.
Understanding the basics of cloud management, including the concept of the cloud, servers, memory, and the ability to define server computation.
Basic knowledge of Restful Services and how they are secured.
Ability to use MS Word, MS Excel and MS PowerPoint.
Proficiency in using MS Paint to create rough sketches of UI screens tailored for customers and various application personas.
Strong oral and written communication skills, with a desire to discuss, debate, and share thoughts with others.

projects.title: Public Equity Investing in Artificial Intelligence

content.text: Explore the dynamics of public equity investing in the artificial intelligence (AI) sector by analyzing key technology companies and financial statements, developing critical insights into AI's economic and investment potential.

Artificial intelligence is transforming industries and markets, making it a hot topic for public equity investors. In this Build Project, you will assume the role of a public equity analyst, focusing on AI technology companies in the semiconductor, software, and internet sectors. You will gain a practical understanding of the tasks entry-level equity analysts perform, by developing skills in fundamental analysis, including business, financial, and qualitative analysis, to determine whether AI stocks represent a long-term growth opportunity or a speculative bubble. The workshops will be interactive with group activities to discuss whether an AI company is a good or bad business, hand-on valuation exercises, and watching videos of what experts have addressed to discuss the current state of AI developments.

By the end of the project, you will have produced a simple stock pitch and prepared for job interviews in the public equity space, with experience tackling the types of questions typically asked in interviews for analyst roles.
Learn how to conduct a fundamental equity research project and understand different investing styles.
Analyze financial statements and KPIs of AI-focused public companies.
Conduct qualitative analysis through earnings call reviews and competitive landscape evaluation.
Apply valuation methodologies to assess the investment potential of technology stocks.
Compare AI investment trends with historical bubbles like dot-com and cryptocurrencies.
Develop and present a stock pitch for an AI company, analyzing whether it is a long or short investment opportunity.
You will get to choose  their own company to present.
Produce a stock presentation slide deck detailing the business analysis, financial performance, qualitative assessment, and valuation of a selected AI-focused public company.

projects.title: Public Equity Valuation & Investment Recommendation

content.text: Evaluate a publicly traded company by combining macro indicators with firm‑level fundamentals to deliver a polished pitch deck investment recommendation.

Detailed analyses and accurate predictions based on fundamental understanding of a company are key to becoming a successful public equity investing professional. In this Build Project, you will wear the hat of a fundamental analyst and develop investment recommendations about a publicly traded company’s stock. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you will dive deep into understanding the company’s business model, evaluating its business strategies and competitive landscapes, analyzing its financial data, and predicting its future growth potential. 

You will also become familiar with tools such as Python to conduct statistical analysis on macroeconomic data and apply various valuation methods in Excel to support your investment theses. The analytical and modeling skills gained from this project will help you become more competitive in the recruiting process for a junior equity investment role.
Interpret Financial Models: Learn how to read and analyze company financial models effectively.
Use Macroeconomic Data with Python: Apply statistical analysis using Python to assess the business environment a company operates in.
Build Valuation Models in Excel: Create detailed financial models to determine the fair value of a company’s publicly traded stock.
Present Investment Theses: Develop and deliver a PowerPoint presentation that combines quantitative and qualitative analysis to support your investment recommendations.
Interest in the financial market (e.g. tracking daily market news through reputable sources) and willingness to perform detailed due diligence
Basic skills and experiences with Excel and PowerPoint
Experience with basic Python (conditions, loops, pandas, matplotlib) or another statistical/coding tool

projects.title: Build & Optimize Your Own Quant Portfolio with Factor Models

content.text: Work hands‑on with real market data as you use Python to turn financial insights into a polished GitHub project and a professional‑style investment pitch you can showcase to recruiters.

In today’s investment industry, entry-level analysts are expected to forecast asset returns, quantify risks, and build data-driven portfolios — skills that power nearly every quant finance and asset management team. In this Build Project, you’ll wear the hat of a quantitative analyst and build a full portfolio construction pipeline, from modeling expected returns with factor models to optimizing portfolio allocations. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you’ll analyze real financial data, estimate factor exposures, run forecasting models, and implement portfolio optimization strategies. You’ll become familiar with industry-standard tools and methodologies like Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), Fama–French three-factor model, Python, pandas, statsmodels, and cvxpy — all within an environment that simulates the operations of a real quant research team.
Calculate asset returns and risks using Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) and Fama–French three-factor model.
Estimate factor exposures and forecast expected returns and covariances from historical data using Python.
Optimize portfolio allocations under realistic constraints with cvxpy to achieve desired risk-return profiles.
Evaluate portfolio performance using metrics such as Sharpe ratio, drawdown, and tracking error.
Communicate investment strategies through clear data-driven reports and presentations.
Knowledge of Python programming: you should be able to write simple functions, work with pandas dataframes, and create basic visualizations using matplotlib.

Understanding of linear regression and statistics: you should be able to interpret regression coefficients, run simple models (as taught in classes like Intro to Statistics or Quantitative Methods), and understand concepts like R^2, residuals, and significance.

Familiarity with financial concepts of return, risk, and diversification: you should know how to calculate returns from price data, understand standard deviation as a risk measure, and explain why diversification reduces risk.
Problem-solving mindset and willingness to learn: you should be ready to debug code, search for solutions, and adapt your approach when facing new challenges.
No prior experience in quantitative investing is needed: we will build the skill together during the project.
Communication and collaboration skills: you should be able to explain your process and results clearly to peers and give/receive constructive feedback.

projects.title: Revolutionizing Cancer Treatment: Innovative Cellular Immunotherapy Strategies

content.text: Explore the current landscape of cell-based cancer immunotherapies and propose an innovative immunotherapy approach that addresses an unmet patient need.

Under the guidance of an experienced industry specialist, you will learn fundamental concepts and processes relevant to the development of cell-based immunotherapy products. This is an excellent opportunity for early researchers to delve into the science behind cell-based immunotherapies and get exposure to relevant skills crucial for research-based roles in this field.
Dissect the current industry trends in relation to cell-based immunotherapies.
Understand fundamental mechanisms underlying cell-based immunotherapies.
Identify key experimental processes, assays, tools and analyses applied in development of cell-based immunotherapies.
Apply industry insights to propose a theoretical cell-based immunotherapy candidate that addresses a current gap in the market.

A basic understanding of immunology, including the immune system, antigen recognition, and immune cell types (helpful but not essential).
Familiarity with reading and comprehending scientific literature.
Experience using Microsoft PowerPoint.

projects.title: Risk & Return: Making Investments in Equity Securities

content.text: Learn how professional investors evaluate, model, and discuss investment opportunities.

Pensions, colleges, and nations across the world rely on investment firms to generate financial returns to support the long-term needs of their retirees, students, and citizens. In this Build Project, you'll learn how investors decide to invest in businesses by donning the hat of an analyst entering an investment firm that is in the process of acquiring a public company. Under the guidance of an experienced industry expert, you will identify a potential investment opportunity, analyze the company's performance, and build an Excel financial model to value it. You'll synthesize your findings to create your own investment memo in PowerPoint—skills critical to succeeding in entry-level roles across financial planning, accounting, banking, investment management and consulting. Entry-level roles in such fields typically pay upwards of $60-80K per year.
Understand and calculate the key financial metrics investors use to evaluate businesses, using a variety of data sources.
Build forecasts and financial models in Microsoft Excel to help value businesses and investments.
Prepare and present investment memorandums to describe and support potential investment opportunities.
A basic understanding of accounting principles (e.g., revenue, cost of goods sold, EBITDA) and finance concepts (e.g., equity, debt).
Some existing exposure to basic statistical concepts (mean, median, mode, quartiles, etc.) and data visualization techniques (bar graphs, bubble plots, etc.).
Past experience using Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets (experience performing basic sums, products, etc.).
An interest in financial markets, and a desire to develop the “investor toolkit” and learn how professional investors evaluate investment opportunities.

projects.title: Risk & Return: Turning Data Into Business Decisions

content.text: Build a professional decision-making slide deck using real data to recommend a business action.

Businesses make decisions every day based on limited information, imperfect data, and tight timelines. In this Build Project, you’ll step into the role of a junior analyst or product thinker and develop a data-driven recommendation for a real business question.

You will design a simple experiment or survey, collect and analyze data using basic probability and statistics, and interpret your findings to understand what the data does and does not show. Using your analysis, you will build a professional decision-making slide deck with Gamma AI that clearly communicates your reasoning and recommendation to a non-technical audience.

Throughout the project, you’ll practice the same skills used in entry-level analytics, business strategy, and product roles: framing questions, working with real data, evaluating tradeoffs, and presenting insights with confidence. By the end of the project, you’ll have a portfolio-ready decision deck you can share in interviews to demonstrate how you turn data into actionable business decisions.
Frame a real-world business question as a clear, testable hypothesis.
Design and run a simple experiment or survey to collect relevant data.
Apply basic probability and statistics to analyze and interpret results.
Translate data findings into a clear business recommendation.
Communicate insights effectively to a non-technical audience using a professional slide deck.
Introductory exposure to probability or statistics, at the level of an introductory college course, including ideas like averages, percentages, and basic comparisons.
Comfort working with spreadsheets (Excel or Google Sheets), such as entering data, calculating simple metrics, and creating basic charts.
Ability to think through problems step by step and explain your reasoning clearly, even if your analysis is not perfect.
Basic written and verbal communication skills, including a willingness to present ideas and receive feedback.
Curiosity about how businesses use data to make decisions, rather than prior industry experience.

projects.title: Scaling Stem Cell Culture: Biotech Industry Practices

content.text: Explore the principles and methodologies behind scaling stem cell differentiation processes from lab to production, preparing for real-world biotech applications.

Stem cell therapy is a growing field in the biotech industry, while the tech transfer from a research proven concept to large scale manufacturing remains a challenge in industry operations. In this Build Project, you’ll wear the hat of a Process Development research associate and design a scaled-up stem cell differentiation process, focusing on maintaining cell quality and consistency. By the end of the 8-weeks project, you will develop a process design in the form of a PowerPoint presentation based on an established stem cell differentiation research protocol. Showcase a flowchart in presentation of the overall process including equipment selection, analytical method, and manufacturing strategy. Under the guidance of an experienced industry expert, you will tackle challenges such as process optimization, equipment selection, and compliance with regulatory standards. This project offers exposure to industry tools like bioreactor design, process modeling, and quality control techniques, simulating real-world biotech industry operations.b:
Design a process for scaling stem cell culture and differentiation into final products.
Evaluate bioreactors suitable for stem cell differentiation processes.
Evaluate challenges and implement strategies for maintaining cell viability, differentiation consistency, and quality during scale-up.
Understand regulatory and quality assurance requirements in cell therapy biomanufacturing.
Basic knowledge of stem cells, including its regenerative ability and applications in medicine.

projects.title: Ship Better Code, Faster: Optimize Developer Workflows with CI/CD and AI

content.text: Analyze, measure, and improve a real software system’s development pipeline by applying developer experience principles, CI/CD automation, and AI-assisted engineering practices.

In this project, you will step into the role of a platform engineer and work hands-on with a real-world software codebase to make it faster, more reliable, and easier to use. You’ll investigate why the current system is slow and frustrating by measuring performance, identifying bottlenecks, and uncovering root causes. Then you will implement practical improvements using CI/CD automation, developer tooling, and AI-assisted coding. Along the way, you’ll build skills in analyzing workflows, improving team efficiency, and making data-driven decisions. Each session blends guided instruction with collaborative problem-solving, giving you experience similar to what engineers do in industry. By the end, you’ll have a portfolio-ready project that demonstrates your ability to improve how software gets built and delivered – skills that are highly relevant for careers in software engineering, DevOps, and platform engineering.
Analyze how a software project moves from code to deployment, and identify where time and effort are being lost using real data.
Construct and configure a CI/CD pipeline using tools like GitHub Actions to automate testing, building, and deployment.
Apply developer experience principles to reduce onboarding friction and improve daily development workflows through scripting and tooling improvements.
Use AI coding tools effectively while evaluating their output for quality, accuracy, and long-term maintainability.
Design a metrics-driven improvement proposal that quantifies engineering impact using industry-standard measurements such as cycle time, build duration, and deployment frequency.
Knowledge in at least one programming language (preferred: JavaScript/TypeScript; acceptable: Python, Java, etc.) including functions, control flow, data structures, and basic file I/O operations.
A working understanding of Git, including how to clone a repository, create branches, commit changes, and open pull requests.
Ability to navigate a command-line interface to execute build scripts, run test suites, and inspect log output.
A general understanding of how web applications work (for example, how the frontend, backend, and database interact).
Willingness to collaborate, troubleshoot challenges, and share your thinking with others during group discussions and presentations.

projects.title: Signals in the Data: Unlocking Hidden Marketing Insights

content.text: Learn how to turn messy Marketing Data into clear insights that boost campaign results.

Is direct mail dead? Not quite. In fact, when done right, direct mail can outperform digital campaigns in customer engagement and response. In this Build Project, you’ll play the role of a marketing analyst for a company running direct mail campaigns across multiple creative variations and customer segments. You'll work with campaign data that will include metrics like response rates, cost per response, and ROI by audience type and creative offerings. Using Excel and/or Power BI, you'll build a compelling dashboard to track how well each campaign performed and where future mailings should be focused. This project will help you gain skills that would lead to entry-level roles.
Understand and analyze key performance indicators or metrics like conversions, response rate, cost per acquisition, return on ad spending.
Visualize performance across various factors (audiences, segments, offer types, etc.…) through Dashboard.
Clean and prepare mail campaign data using data cleaning tools such as Excel or SQL, and analyze using visualization tools such as Power BI and Tableau, and Excel.
Prepare and present final findings in a concise, executive style dashboard and summary.
A basic understanding of marketing concepts (e.g., conversions, response rates, return on incrementality, return on ad spends)
Some existing exposure to data visualization techniques (bar graphs, pie charts, etc.)
Prior basic experience with Microsoft Excel (Pivot Table, Formulas, Filters) and Data Visualization Tools such as Power BI or Tableau (Good to have)
Basic ability to summarize insights and recommendations clearly in a written or visual report mainly Microsoft PowerPoint.

projects.title: SmartLeave: A Java-Based Employee Leave and Risk Management System

content.text: A Java-based application that streamlines employee leave management while assessing IT-related risks from absenteeism and access control to enhance organizational security and efficiency.

This Build project introduces you to practical software development by building a simplified Java application that manages employee leave requests and identifies basic IT risks related to segregation of duties (SoD).  Through the course of 8 workshops, you will implement core features such as employee data handling, leave tracking, and simple rule-based SoD checks—such as flagging if an employee with access to both approval and processing functions is on leave or returns early. Using Object-Oriented Programming principles, file handling for data storage, and basic report generation, the project offers a hands-on introduction to how technology can support IT governance. Students will also use GitHub for version control and documentation, aligning their skills with industry expectations in software development, audit, and risk management.
Develop a basic Java application using Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) to manage employee leave records.
Implement simple CRUD operations for employees and leave requests with data stored in-memory or using text/CSV files.
Apply basic rule-based logic to flag potential IT risks related to absenteeism and user access roles.
Generate straightforward, text-based reports summarizing leave activity and flagged risks.
Use GitHub to manage your project files, document your work, and present your project in a professional format.

Understanding of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Principles: You will need to understand core OOP concepts such as classes, objects, inheritance, and encapsulation to design a well-structured Java application. This includes defining classes like Employee, LeaveRequest, and RiskAssessment, as well as understanding how to use methods and attributes effectively.

Knowledge of Basic File Handling or Data Persistence: You will need to know how to store and retrieve data using file handling techniques such as reading and writing to CSV or text files, or using an in-memory data structure (like a List or Map). This skill will help manage employee and leave records within the application.

Familiarity with Rule-Based Risk Assessment Logic: You will need to understand how to design simple risk rules for detecting conflicts in roles (Segregation of Duties). For instance, knowing how to check if an employee holds both "Approver" and "Processor" roles at the same time and then flagging that as a potential risk during leave requests.

Basic Report Generation and Data Formatting: You will need the ability to generate and format simple text-based reports summarizing leave requests and identified risks. This involves presenting data in a readable format, such as showing which employees are on leave and if any risk violations were detected due to role conflicts.

Version Control with GitHub:  You will need to be comfortable with Git and GitHub to manage your project's source code, document your process, and share your work. This includes using basic Git commands (e.g., git init, git commit, git push) and organizing your repository with clear documentation of project features and progress.

projects.title: Stop Hallucinations: Build a Fact-Checked AI Knowledge Assistant

content.text: Build a Python service using Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide grounded answers to user questions based on a proprietary knowledge base.

Are you tired of chatbots and virtual assistants that give you confident sounding but completely wrong answers? In this project, you will build a sophisticated knowledge assistant capable of answering complex questions by referencing a defined set of documents (the "Knowledge Base"). You will implement a RAG based software, which solves the critical problem of LLM "hallucination" by supplying factual context from your documents before generating a response. This involves creating a data ingestion pipeline, implementing a vector database to index your knowledge, and orchestrating the retrieval and generation components via Python. The ability to write production-ready code, implement modern LLM architectures such as RAG, and work with vector databases forms the core skill set behind most enterprise GenAI systems today. These capabilities align directly with the competencies sought in ML Engineering and AI/Software Developer roles.

Previous experience about LLM/RAG is not required.

projects.title: Kinesiology in Action! Create an Injury Prevention Plan

content.text: Learn how kinesiology prevents injuries and boosts performance for everyone by assessing a chosen athlete and designing your own injury prevention plans.

Applied kinesiology is the scientific study of human movement, focusing on how the body’s anatomical structures interact to produce efficient and effective motion. In the realm of sport-specific biomechanics, applied kinesiology delves into the mechanics of actions such as sprinting, jumping, and throwing, analyzing how athletes can optimize their movement patterns to maximize performance. By understanding the body’s kinetic chain and muscle function, students learn how to enhance athletic abilities through precise technique adjustments and targeted training programs. Applied kinesiology also plays a crucial role in identifying injury mechanisms—such as overuse, improper form, or biomechanical imbalances—and creating injury prevention strategies that maintain optimal movement efficiency while reducing risk. Rehabilitation and corrective exercises are then used to restore functional movement post-injury, emphasizing balance, strength, and coordination to safely return athletes to peak performance. For students pursuing careers in sports, physical therapy, or health science, applied kinesiology bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application in optimizing human movement.b:["$","

projects.title: Structural Design Optimization for Metal Additive Manufacturing (DFAM)

content.text: Learn how to design and optimize a lightweight metal component using CAD, topology optimization, and basic simulation, following real-world additive manufacturing practices.

In this 8-week Build Project, you will learn how engineers design lightweight, high‑performance metal parts for additive manufacturing. Starting with a simple design problem, you will create a CAD model, apply Design for Additive Manufacturing (DFAM) principles, and use topology optimization to reduce material while maintaining strength. The project also introduces basic structural simulation to verify design performance and simple cost and manufacturability considerations. By the end of the project, you will complete and present a fully optimized metal AM component, gaining hands‑on experience with tools and workflows used in modern mechanical design and advanced manufacturing roles.

Perform iterative topology optimization to maximize the stiffness-to-weight ratio while achieving significant mass reduction.
Conduct cross-solver structural validation to ensure design integrity and consistency between Altair and SolidWorks.
Transform organic optimization results into watertight, manufacturable solids using PolyNURBS-based geometry reconstruction.
Ability to create basic 3D parts using CAD software such as SolidWorks or Fusion 360.

projects.title: The Intelligent investor: Security Analysis and Value Investing

content.text: Develop a stock pitch – an investment thesis backed by data and analysis to support a recommendation, incorporating valuation metrics and a discussion of potential catalysts and risks associated with the investment.

This Build Project is designed to give you a strong foundation in the value investing process, an investment philosophy that guided legendary investors like Warren Buffet and Mario Gabelli. It’s an investment approach that helps investors identify, research, and buy securities priced well below their true market value. In this Build Project, you will pick up tools and strategies to collect and analyze information as well as an integrated framework that teaches you how to identify opportunities for investment that others may miss. Knowing the basics of Warren Buffet’s philosophy is a must for starting an investment career, no matter what type of investing you are interested in and what asset class. This project will be most valuable for students looking to go into investment management, investment banking or corporate finance.
By the end of the project, you will be able to:
- Apply the value investing principles to make smart, rational investment decisions.
- Learn to calculate asset value and earnings power value to understand the underlying value of a security.
- Conduct a strategic analysis of a company to understand its ability to produce ongoing profits through developing a company specific Excel model.

- Develop a stock pitch, a write-up that argues for or against investing in a public company's stock, and which is backed by a strong investment thesis, data, valuation metrics, catalysts, and an assessment of the risk factors.
For you to be successful in this project, you will need:
- Experience with market research and economic analysis (e.g. has taken minimum 1–2 economics or accounting classes in college, working on a business degree, etc.)
- Knowledge of financial statements and accounting (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement and how they flow into one another)
- A strong interest in finance and investment management
- Basic knowledge of Excel (you should know the formulas like sum(), product())

projects.title: The Ticker's Heart: Build a High-Performance Financial Order Engine

content.text: Implement a high-performance matching engine from scratch to process and execute financial derivative orders.

In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Trading Systems Engineer and build a high-performance matching engine, capable of processing and executing live trade orders. This low-latency system is the core component of modern financial markets, from the NYSE to crypto exchanges, making these skills essential for top-tier entry-level roles in quantitative trading firms. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll learn how to design and develop complex, ordered data structures, manage a real-time order book, and process different order types based on strict price-time priority rules. You'll become familiar with industry techniques like low-latency programming and algorithmic optimization to ensure your engine can handle high-frequency order flow.
Implement the core data structures (e.g., price-level trees, linked lists) for an efficient limit order book.
Design the matching logic (e.g., Price-Time priority) for common order types like 'Limit', 'Market', and 'IOC' (Immediate-or-Cancel).
Analyze and optimize the system for low latency, focusing on efficient data handling, algorithmic complexity, and avoiding performance bottlenecks.
Develop a simple network protocol (e.g., over TCP/UDP) to submit orders and receive trade execution reports.
Map out and evaluate the core system architecture of modern financial exchanges and trading systems

Intermediate High-Performance Programming (Python, C++): You should be comfortable building a multi-file application. This includes a solid understanding of object-oriented concepts (classes/structs), memory management (pointers, references, or garbage collection), and basic file I/O.

Knowledge of Data Structures & Algorithms: You need knowledge at the level of a typical Data Structures and Algorithms university course. You must be able to explain the performance trade-offs (Big O notation) of hash maps, linked lists, and trees, and be comfortable implementing them.
Basic Development & Version Control: You should be able to compile and run your code from a command line and know how to use Git to clone, commit, and push your work to a repository.
Understanding of Concurrency Concepts: You don't need to be an expert, but you should be able to explain what a thread, a race condition, and a mutex are.
Analytical Problem-Solving: This project involves complex logic. You should be comfortable debugging step-by-step and have a persistent approach to solving challenging bugs.

projects.title: TweetLens: Unveiling Insights from Twitter Data

All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real analytics team, preparing you for the fast-paced world of data analysis and visualization.

Create insightful visualizations to identify trends and patterns in Twitter data.

projects.title: Uncover Urban Travel Patterns Through Ride-Share Data

content.text: Build an interactive Colab notebook that transforms raw ride-sharing data into actionable insights for product and business decisions.

Understanding data and turning it into actionable insights is at the heart of how today’s tech and mobility companies make business decisions, and entry-level data roles often focus on analyzing ride patterns, customer behavior, and operational performance.

In this Build project, you’ll wear the hat of a Product Data Analyst at a ride-sharing company and develop an interactive Colab notebook that uncovers ride patterns, evaluates ride growth, and predicts ride cancellations. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you’ll clean and organize the data, run applied statistical tests, define product KPIs such as ride volume growth and average revenue per ride, and train a simple predictive model to estimate ride cancellations based on time and location features. You’ll become familiar with industry-standard tools and methods like Python, pandas, data visualization libraries, and predictive modeling techniques. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real data science and analytics team, supporting business stakeholders with insights that drive data-informed decisions.
Clean, manage, and query real-world mobility data using Python.
Use applied statistics and hypothesis testing (confidence intervals, t-tests, descriptive analytics) to answer questions about ride patterns and fares.
Define and compute product analytics KPIs such as ride volume growth, average revenue per ride, retention proxies, and funnel conversion rates.
Use predictive modeling to understand user behavior based on historic data.
Design clear and human-centered data visualizations (time-series plots, heatmaps, funnel charts) that communicate insights effectively to technical and non-technical audiences.

projects.title: Understanding principles of biochemical genetics with computational biology

content.text: Apply advanced biochemistry and bioinformatics techniques to solve problems in drug discovery and genomic integrity research through virtual pipelines.

This Build Project provides undergraduate students with a comprehensive, hands-on experience in translational biochemistry and computational biology, focusing on real-world applications in drug discovery and genomic integrity. You will engage in designing and analyzing CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screens using next-generation sequencing (NGS), develop virtual pipelines for structural variant detection using Optical Genome Mapping (OGM), and perform protein abundance analysis from LC-MS data using R. Through guided supervision, you will gain practical experience with industry-standard tools and databases such as dbVAR, and ClinVar, while also learning to synthesize their findings into professional scientific reports. The project bridges fundamental biochemical principles with bioinformatics and emerging genomic technologies to prepare students for careers in biotechnology and biomedical research.
Design and implement CRISPR knockout screening pipelines using next-generation sequencing (NGS) data and tools such as BWA, Samtools, and CRISPResso.
Analyze structural variants using Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) and interpret findings with reference databases like dbVAR, ClinVar, and gnomAD.
Quantify protein abundance using LC-MS data and perform statistical analysis in R, including visualization with heatmaps and volcano plots.
Translate genomic and proteomic data into biologically meaningful insights relevant to drug discovery, particularly in identifying oncogenes and therapeutic targets.
Develop publication-quality reports and visualizations that effectively communicate research findings to scientific and industry audiences.
A solid understanding of DNA structure and function, including how mutations such as insertions, deletions, and structural variants affect gene expression and protein function.

Familiarity with the central dogma of molecular biology (DNA > RNA > Protein), and how CRISPR-Cas9 edits the genome by inducing double-strand breaks followed by DNA repair mechanisms like NHEJ and HDR.
Basic experience with data analysis tools such as Excel or R, especially for generating plots and interpreting trends from tabular datasets (e.g., variant counts or protein abundances).
The ability to interpret scientific figures (e.g., heatmaps, volcano plots, gene models) and translate data into concise written conclusions.
Willingness to explore new bioinformatics tools and databases (such as COSMIC, gnomAD, and ClinVar) with guided instruction and troubleshooting support.

projects.title: Understanding Various Mammalian Species Through the World of Zoology

content.text: Investigate the Zoology world through various mammalian species and apply it to the species of your choice by writing an academic paper and presenting your work to your peers.

Welcome to the extraordinary world of mammals. From the echolocation of bats to the beautiful songs of whales across the oceans, to small nocturnal creatures and the social lives of primates or lions, mammals reveal nature through a complex and captivating lens. Through years of evolution, survival, intelligence, and adaptation - we will explore not only how mammals live but why they thrive in such astonishing diversity. In this Build Project, you will explore mammalian ecology and the diverse biomes these species inhabit across the globe. You will learn to identify these biomes as the ecological context shaping your chosen species and its survival strategies. The project examines interspecies relationships, phenotypic and genotypic adaptations, and real-world human–wildlife conflict, highlighting the impacts of human activity on mammalian species. You will also address the care of mammals in captive environments. Through eight guided virtual workshops and the instructor’s hands-on field experience in the African bushfield, you will develop a professional APA- or MLA-style research paper focused on a species of your choice. By the end of the project, you will gain a strong, applied understanding of your chosen species in both captive and natural settings. b:["
Identify key biomes including biomes found within Southern Africa
Troubleshoot and address conservation issues
Gain extensive knowledge on the honey badger and your own species of study
Understand the ecology of the African “bushveld” including key ecological factors of your own species of study
Write an academic paper of your own and learn how to present it in an academic setting
Know how to secure a future in the Zoological field
Earned strong grades in their introductory biology courses, ensuring a foundational understanding of the principles of biology and their applications in wildlife management and zoology.
Be prepared to identify and address complex ecological issues, such as poaching, habitat degradation, and biodiversity loss, both locally and globally.

Proficiency in ecology will be essential for recognizing and explaining the interdependence within ecosystems, while skills in mammalogy and invertebrate zoology will aid in distinguishing between species and understanding their ecological niches.
Apply evolutionary biology to evaluate species adaptations, identify pressing conservation challenges, and propose scientifically sound solutions.
This project is suited for a beginner striving Zoologist entering the field. However, all students with an interest in conversation and animal wellbeing can thrive within this project.

projects.title: Underwriting the Underwriters: The GP Stakes Playbook

content.text: Analyze a private equity firm the way professional investors do, building a financial model, a valuation, and an investment memo you can showcase to future employers.

Private equity now manages over $8 trillion, and a fast-growing corner of the industry invests in the Private Equity (PE) firms themselves rather than their funds — a strategy called GP stakes, used by firms like Blue Owl and Blackstone. In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a GP stakes analyst and research, model, value, and pitch an investment in a private equity firm. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll build a one-page company tear sheet, an Excel model of the firm's economics, a valuation with scenarios, and a 5-slide investment memo. You'll become familiar with industry tools and techniques like fee-related earnings (FRE) modeling, comparable multiples, DCF valuation, and Investment Committee memo writing. All this will happen in an environment that simulates the operations of a real investment team, ending with a live pitch to a simulated Investment Committee.

Explain what GP stakes investing is, why investors like Blue Owl and Blackstone buy minority stakes in private equity firms, and how this strategy fits into the broader alternative asset management industry.
Evaluate a private equity firm as an investment target by analyzing its strategy, fund history, team, and AUM trajectory
Understand how private equity firms make money, including management fees, carried interest, and GP investment income.
Construct a structured investment argument, articulating the drivers, risks, and mitigants of an investment decision the way analysts do in an Investment Committee memo.
Basic knowledge of Excel: you should be able to write formulas like SUM and IF, link cells across a sheet, and make a simple chart. We'll teach data tables and sensitivity analysis.
Understanding the time value of money: you should be able to explain why $100 today is worth more than $100 next year, at the level covered in an intro finance or economics course.
Familiarity with basic finance vocabulary (revenue, fees, margins); no private equity experience needed; we'll cover that together.
