projects.title: Unlocking the Genome: Exploring CRISPR-Cas9 and Genotoxicity Concerns

content.text: Exploring Gene Therapy and Genome Editing Technologies with a Focus on CRISPR-Cas9 Mechanism, Ethical Considerations, and Genotoxicity Studies.

This project aims to explore key aspects of gene editing and gene therapy, focusing on current techniques, historical evolution, and the associated challenges. You will delve into the mechanisms and applications of gene editing technologies, understand how they have evolved from early experiments to sophisticated tools used in modern biotechnology and medicine. Utilizing bioinformatics tools, you will conduct an analysis to understand disease modalities, interpreting genomic data to identify and characterize structural variants, and assessing their potential impact on gene function and disease progression.  

The project will also investigate genomic instability and off-target effects that can arise from gene editing, emphasizing their implications for therapeutic safety and efficacy. Additionally, you will explore the role of bioinformatics as a powerful tool for deciphering disease modalities, leveraging computational approaches to analyze genomic data and understand disease mechanisms at a molecular level. 

Through this comprehensive exploration, this Build Project seeks to equip you with a deep understanding of the complexities and potentials of gene editing technologies in healthcare and biotechnology. You will produce a report about the evolution and current state of gene editing techniques, including a historical overview of gene therapy. It will also cover the mechanisms of genomic instability and off-target effects resulting from gene editing, providing insights into their implications for therapeutic safety and efficacy.
Understand current gene editing techniques with an overview of the evolution and history of gene therapy.
Understand genomic instability and off-target mediated effects that occur as a result of gene editing.
Use Bioinformatics as an efficient tool to understand disease modalities.
A Basic understanding of Gene Editing Techniques: Knowledge of how gene editing tools like CRISPR/Cas9 and TALENs work at a basic level, including the concept of targeted DNA modifications.
Familiarity with the significance of gene therapy, its purpose, and basic history, including key milestones such as the first gene therapy trials.
A Basic understanding of the principles of genomic stability and instability, including basic concepts of DNA structure, function, and repair mechanisms.
Familiarity with the basic purpose and function of bioinformatics tools, such as sequence alignment and variant calling.
Basic ability to navigate and use tools like CRISPResso2 for analyzing sequencing data and UCSC Genome Browser for visualizing genomic data.

projects.title: Unveiling Health: Data Discovery Expedition

projects.title: Product, Contracting, and Dollar Flow in the U.S. Healthcare Industry

content.text: Build an overview of product, contracting, and dollar flow between key stakeholders in the U.S. healthcare industry.

The landscape of the US healthcare industry resembles a complex and fragmented puzzle with various types of pieces. Numerous stakeholders, including healthcare providers, insurance companies, pharmaceutical manufacturers, and government agencies, contribute to a system that often appears intricate and challenging to navigate. The intricate web of regulations, varying payment structures, and the multitude of players involved can make understanding the flow of dollars, products, and contracts seem like solving a 1000-piece puzzle without edge-pieces. Imagine that a pharmaceutical organization that partners with Company X, has reached out asking for support to provide an overview of the value drivers of key stakeholders in the healthcare industry and the flow of product, dollar, and contracts between these stakeholders that they plan to use to train their salesforce new hires. This information will provide a foundation for their salesforce that will help them navigate conversations with healthcare providers, hospital administrators, and payers. You are part of the Company X team and will have to work on this challenge. In this project, you will first describe the roles, responsibilities, and value drivers of key stakeholders in the healthcare industry including Beneficiaries, Pharmacies, Wholesalers, Payers, Providers, Manufacturers, Funders, and Pharmacy Benefit Managers, and then create a visually appealing flowchart that accurately represents the flow of product, dollar, and contracting between them. This is an opportunity for you to understand the value that each of these stakeholders provide to the healthcare system and how they co-exist to finally provide affordable and quality healthcare services to patients. After completing this project, you will get a deep understanding of the intricacies of the US healthcare industry, develop strong strategic thinking, research, and analytical skills, and improve your ability to communicate your knowledge and insights gathered in a clear, specific, and visually appealing format.

Effectively gather information from credible sources which include scientific literature reviews, government publication database searches, professional organizations, and compendium guideline reviews.

Present the insights in a specific, effective, and comprehensive manner that conveys the key points gathered, tells a story about each of the stakeholders, and ensures the audience is taking away learnings from the presentation.

projects.title: Vendor Performance Analytics with Excel and Power BI

content.text: Use Excel and Power BI to turn quarterly sales data into simple, clear visuals to help with making decisions.

Ready to help a tech reseller figure out how its vendors are doing? Use Excel and Power BI to turn quarterly sales data into simple, clear visuals. No experience needed—just a curiosity about how businesses use data to make decisions!

Tech resellers work with vendors to sell products like gadgets or software, but keeping track of who’s selling what can be a puzzle. In this Build Project, you’ll step into the role of a junior analyst for a fictional reseller. Starting with a spreadsheet, you’ll clean it up, add up the numbers, and create a dashboard to show which vendors are shining and which need a boost. Using Excel, you’ll tidy up quarterly sales and margin data, then use Power BI to make visuals that answer questions like “Which vendor is growing?” or “Where are profits slipping?” By the end, you’ll have a dashboard that could help a manager make smarter calls and proven skills that can kickstart your data analyst career!

projects.title: Venture Fund Investing: Aligning Founders and Institutional Investors

content.text: Develop an understanding of the fundamental principles that drive Venture Capital fund investing and get insights into ways to bridge the incentives gap between entrepreneurs and institutional investors.

Innovation is powered by funding yet the relationship between startup founders and investors is often marked by misaligned incentives and conflicting interests. Receiving funding from reputable Venture Capital (VC) firms is a strong positive signal of success for any entrepreneur, yet many founders could benefit from gaining a deeper understanding of what institutional VC investors look for when identifying their next big investment opportunity.

In this Build Project, you will put yourself in the position of a private institutional investor and analyze the performance factors of a successful venture portfolio, practice negotiating a term sheet, and develop an investment memo pitching a compelling startup investment opportunity to an Investment Committee. With the guidance of a professional with private institutional investing experience, you will calculate a venture portfolio’s performance metrics and practice identifying and pitching startup investments. You will master the fundamentals of key startup valuation metrics and portfolio management basics such as calculating pre-/post-money valuations, portfolio performance metrics, and others. This project will stimulate the operations of a venture capital firm and provide holistic insights into the skills both venture investors and founders need for success in the competitive venture ecosystem.
b:

projects.title: Visualizing Supply Chain Stability: Power BI's Role in Inventory Risk Management

content.text: Develop a Power BI solution to analyze inventory risks, streamline stock management, and drive proactive decision-making to enhance supply chain resilience.

Embark on an engaging journey into the world of industrial engineering and operations optimization. This Build Project presents an exciting opportunity to address key challenges in inventory and warehouse operations management. By developing a PowerBI dashboard, you'll gain practical experience in analyzing inventory levels, assessing risks, and proactively optimizing supply chain parameters to improve operational resilience. You'll focus on applying industrial engineering principles to enhance inventory management strategies, streamline processes, and boost overall warehouse and manufacturing efficiency.

These skills are highly transferable, making them valuable not only in the supply chain and logistics sectors but also in industries such as manufacturing, consulting, hospitality, and beyond. This hands-on experience will provide you with the critical skills needed for a successful career in operations optimization, setting you apart in a variety of industries.
Develop a Power BI dashboard to monitor inventory levels, assess risk exposure, and create proactive strategies for inventory risk mitigation in warehouse and manufacturing environments.
Analyze data using Power BI to forecast demand variability, optimize inventory policies, and adjust supply chain parameters to improve operational resilience.
Apply advanced analytics techniques in Power BI to identify inefficiencies, recommend improvements, and drive data-driven decision-making for inventory management and supply chain optimization.
Propose industrial engineering solutions to enhance warehouse and manufacturing performance, focusing on inventory control, resource allocation, and process optimization.
Basic Excel knowledge: including the use of formulas, sorting, filtering, and manipulating data.
Basic knowledge of industrial engineering concepts: which is helpful but not required.
Basic proficiency in data analysis and visualization tools: preferred but not mandatory.

projects.title: Vital Components of Adult Hearing Care

content.text: Explore hearing loss mechanisms and use cutting-edge research to educate adults on its impact, treatment options, tinnitus management, and hearing protection.

Hearing loss is increasingly prevalent among adults, particularly older individuals. Research has highlighted its severe effects, including increased risk of falls, depression, cognitive decline, dementia, and higher rates of hospitalization. Despite these significant impacts, public awareness about the importance of adult hearing care remains low, with fewer than 20% of adults with hearing loss seeking treatment. 

In this project, you will create an awareness overview resource aimed at educating the public on crucial aspects of adult hearing care. Your presentation will cover: the mechanisms and pathways of hearing, the pathologies and impacts of hearing loss, the characteristics and management of tinnitus, options for hearing devices, and strategies for hearing protection. This project will not only immerse you in the field of audiology but also provide you with valuable experience in advocacy and research. Developing the ability to critically review research literature is essential for evidence-based practice. The skills and knowledge gained from this project will be vital for your success in the healthcare field.

Elaborate on hearing pathways from peripheral to central level. Identify the anatomical regions of the ear, including outer ear, middle ear, and inner ear and explain each ear region’s function. Understand the function of the auditory nerve and how sound signals are delivered to the central brain level.

Classify 3 types of hearing loss and interpret hearing loss degree and configurations that are reflected on the audiograms. The 3 types of hearing loss include: Conductive, Sensorineural, and Mixed hearing loss. Learn the concepts of audiogram, frequency, hearing level in decibel, hearing thresholds, air conduction testing, bone conduction testing, and symbols to document results on audiogram.
Critically review research literatures that investigate the impact of hearing loss, especially on cognitive function.
Differentiate non-surgical and surgical hearing device options. Understand the differences regarding device working mechanism, suitable population, and the general process of device fitting.
Explain tinnitus definitions, correlation of tinnitus and hearing loss, and management options for tinnitus.
Understanding the meaning of hearing impairment.
Familiarity with physical concepts of mass, elasticity, sound source, media, energy, work, frequency, sound intensity, density, sound waveforms.
Familiarity with concepts of transducer (e.g. headphones, microphones, speaker).
Memory in your cell phone to download and utilize designated applications.
Experience with Microsoft PowerPoint, Microsoft Word.

projects.title: Weather or Marketing: What Really Drives Sales?

content.text: Investigate real anonymized e-commerce data in Python to uncover whether weather or marketing truly drives sales, presenting your verdict to a simulated executive team.

Modern brands are drowning in data but starving for real insights: a marketing team may celebrate a campaign that "drove" sales that were actually caused by a heat wave. In this Build Project, you'll wear the hat of a Data Scientist at a fast-growing e-commerce company and investigate what truly moves sales. Under the supervision of an experienced industry expert, you'll get hands-on with real, anonymized sales data: cleaning it, merging in regional weather data, visualizing patterns, and building a regression model. Then discover why that model can mislead executives, and see how data scientists use causal inference to find the truth. You'll become familiar with industry tools like pandas, seaborn, and statsmodels, all in an environment that simulates how a real data science team turns raw data into executive decisions. No prior causal inference experience needed: every concept is taught from the ground up. You'll finish with two resume ready deliverables: a polished Jupyter Notebook showcasing your full analysis, and an executive slide deck you'll present live to a simulated leadership team.
Explore, clean, and merge real-world business datasets in Python using pandas.
Create clear visualizations with seaborn/matplotlib to reveal patterns between weather, marketing spend, and sales.
Fit and interpret a multiple linear regression with statsmodels, and explain what its coefficients do.
Explain why correlation is not causation, spot confounding variables, and interpret the results of a causal analysis (propensity score matching).
Turn data findings into business recommendations and present them to a simulated executive team using data storytelling.

Some experience with Python: you should be able to write loops and functions and have used a library like pandas or numpy at least once. (taking an intro programming or data course should be sufficient)
Basic familiarity with tabular data: loading a CSV, filtering rows/columns, handling missing values, exploratory data analysis, etc. (We will practive together as well)
Exposure to introductory statistics: you should recognize concepts like mean, distribution, correlation, and simple linear regression (one intro stats course is enough).
Curiosity to question data: a willingness to ask "does X really cause Y, or is something else going on?"
No causal inference or machine learning experience required — all of it is taught from scratch.

projects.title: Web Security 101: Find and Secure Common Vulnerabilities

content.text: Explore and exploit real-world web vulnerabilities through hands-on labs, learning how attackers break applications and how to defend them.

Web application vulnerabilities are among the most common and persistent security issues across modern software systems, and identifying them is a core responsibility in many entry-level cybersecurity and application security roles. In this Build Project, you will step into the role of a junior security analyst and actively analyze and document real-world web vulnerabilities by performing hands-on exploitation and risk assessment. Under the guidance of an experienced industry professional, you will work with intentionally vulnerable web applications to intercept traffic, manipulate inputs, construct proof-of-concept attacks, and clearly document how and why these weaknesses can be abused. Throughout the project, you will apply industry-standard tools and techniques such as Burp Suite, browser developer tools, HTTP request analysis, and payload crafting to explore vulnerabilities including SQL injection, cross-site scripting, authentication flaws, Cross-Site Request Forgery, path traversal, and insecure Cross-Origin Resource Sharing configurations. All work will take place in a structured environment that mirrors the workflow of a real-world web security or penetration testing team, emphasizing professional documentation, ethical testing practices, and clear communication of security findings.

🚨 This is a project exclusive for CCSF Cybersecurity students who are eligible for a stipend upon completion. For more information about this, please contact Steve Nelson at snelson@ccsf.edub:[
Identify and exploit common web vulnerabilities such as SQL Injection, Authentication flaws, Path Traversal, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), CSRF, and CORS misconfigurations.
Explore industry-standard tools including Burp Suite, browser developer tools, and basic scripting to analyze traffic, craft payloads, and test for security weaknesses.
Examine the browser security model (cookies, sessions, same-origin policy) and how attackers bypass it.
Propose and justify secure coding practices and configurations that prevent each vulnerability type.
Role-play and model the professional documenting strategies of an entry-level security analyst or penetration tester.
HTTP Concepts: Ability to describe and explain the concepts of requests, responses, parameters, and  cookies.

Web Browser Developer Tools: Ability to use the Network tab for inspecting web traffic (HTTP requests/responses) and the Console for debugging and interacting with scripts (e.g., logging variables, running simple JavaScript).
HTML & URLs: Knowledge of how data is transmitted via forms, parameters, and links.
SQL Fundamentals: Familiarity with basic database commands (e.g., SELECT, FROM, WHERE) to understand SQL Injection vulnerabilities.
Web Markup (HTML/JavaScript): Understanding how HTML renders content and how JavaScript executes within the browser (essential for comprehending XSS attacks).

projects.title: Why we get old and how to measure it: a computational analysis of aging biomarkers

content.text: Biomarkers of aging have been notoriously difficult to find. In this Build Project, you will analyze real-world biological data to find good ones.

As long as humans have existed, they have tried to live longer. But today, the combination of large-scale ‘omics data and machine learning may help us unlock some of the secrets behind why we get old, and what we can do about it.

In this Build Project, you'll assume the role of a Computational Biologist, analyzing methylomics data to identify novel biomarkers of aging. During the Build Project, we will cover the theory behind the field of aging biology, which you will then use to build models. You will retrieve, clean, and process omics data, apply machine learning models for data analysis, and produce scientific figures. It is assumed that you have familiarity with biology OR data science (ideally both). If you don’t have experience with one of them, you can still enroll but you will need to learn on your own to get the most out of the project.
By the end of the project, you will be able to:  Have a good understanding of the field of aging biology, including what biomarkers exist.
Perform data analysis using Python and machine learning techniques.
Create visualizations and reproducible scientific figures.
Develop a comprehensive analysis pipeline in Jupyter Notebooks.
Present findings in a professional scientific format.
Experience with Python programming.
Familiarity with basic statistics and data science.
Experience running Jupyter notebooks.
College-level understanding of molecular biology.
Experience with reading scientific papers.

projects.title: Wired Differently: Decoding the Neurodivergent Mind

content.text: Explore the science behind neurodivergent brains and design an evidence-based toolkit that supports diverse cognitive profiles across academic, clinical, and workplace settings.

As awareness of neurodiversity grows across industries, the demand for professionals who can translate psychological science into inclusive practices has never been greater. Every brain learns, feels, and thinks in its own unique way and understanding those differences is the key to true inclusion.

In this Build Project, you'll step into the role of a Clinical psychologist, researcher and inclusion strategist, working to bridge the gap between science and real-world accessibility. Under the supervision of an experienced clinical psychology postdoctoral fellow, you'll analyze neurocognitive and behavioral patterns, explore evidence-based interventions, and design an applied Neurodivergence Support Toolkit that empowers individuals and organizations to better support diverse minds. You’ll become familiar with psychological assessment frameworks, inclusive design principles, and applied behavioral strategies used across education, healthcare, and organizational settings, all within a simulated environment that mirrors how psychology translates into real-world impact.

By the end of the project, you’ll create a Neurodivergence Support Toolkit in the form of a short, visually engaging slide deck or one-page PDF. You’ll present your toolkit in a casual, interactive showcase, demonstrating how psychology can be turned into real-world strategies for inclusion and support.
Analyze how differences in brain functioning shape attention, learning, and emotional regulation across neurodivergent profiles.
Evaluate real-world applications of psychological and neurocognitive research to support inclusion in different settings.
Apply evidence-based psychological principles to design practical tools and strategies that empower neurodivergent individuals.
Communicate complex psychological ideas in clear, accessible language through a professional, portfolio-ready deliverable.
Interest in Psychology and Human Behavior: You should be curious about how the brain works, how people learn and regulate emotions, and how these processes differ across individuals.

Basic understanding of research or behavioral science concepts: You should be familiar with ideas such as attention, motivation, learning, or emotional regulation, typically covered in classes like Introduction to Psychology or Human Development.
Good communication and reflection skills: You’ll need to express your thoughts clearly in discussions and reflections and be open to exploring different perspectives.
Empathy and collaboration: You should feel comfortable working in diverse teams, listening to others’ experiences, and engaging with sensitivity and respect.
It’s ideal for students who want to deepen their understanding of neurodiversity and apply psychological principles in real-world, inclusive contexts.

projects.title: Zero-Day Python: Vulnerability Discovery Lab

content.text: A hands-on cybersecurity lab where students use Python scripting and professional tools to detect and report network vulnerabilities while simulating real-world security consulting practices.

Embark on an interactive cybersecurity learning experience where you will use Python and industry-standard tools to simulate the work of an entry-level security analyst. This project focuses on building technical and analytical skills in network scanning, vulnerability discovery, risk mitigation, and professional reporting. Through guided workshops, you will design, test, and present a full vulnerability assessment using tools like Kali Linux, VMware, Python, and standards such as ISO and NIST. This hands-on environment simulates real-world scenarios in cybersecurity operations and consulting.
Develop and execute Python scripts to scan hosts and networks for vulnerabilities using tools like PyShark and socket libraries.
Analyze network infrastructure through OSI/TCP-IP models and identify threat vectors and protocol weaknesses.
Conduct a complete vulnerability assessment, including risk analysis and mitigation strategies based on real-world cases.
Apply ISO and NIST security standards in the context of risk management, disaster recovery, and security planning.
Document findings into a professional-grade technical report and present results in a formal stakeholder setting.
Intermediate Python: loops, conditionals, functions, error handling, and working with libraries like sockets.
Basic understanding of OSI and TCP/IP models and port communication.
Foundational knowledge of vulnerability assessments and scanning principles.
Familiarity with technical documentation and consulting report structure
